examples.text: Eu adorava ouvir o canto do canário.

translations.de: Ich liebte es, dem Gesang des Kanarienvogels zuzuhören.
translations.en: I loved listening to the canary's song.
translations.fr: J'adorais écouter le chant du canari.

examples.text: Os avós trouxeram presentes para os netos.

translations.de: Die Großeltern haben Geschenke für ihre Enkelkinder mitgebracht.
translations.en: The grandparents brought gifts for their grandchildren.
translations.fr: Les grands-parents ont apporté des cadeaux pour leurs petits-enfants.

examples.text: Todas as guerras são absurdas e abomináveis.

translations.de: Alle Kriege sind absurd und abscheulich.
translations.en: All wars are absurd and abominable.
translations.fr: Toutes les guerres sont absurdes et abominables.

examples.text: Eu ouço e leio os diálogos repetidamente.

translations.de: Ich höre und lese die Dialoge immer wieder.
translations.en: I listen to and read the dialogues repeatedly.
translations.fr: J'écoute et je lis les dialogues à plusieurs reprises.

more.definition: the (the definite grammatical article that shows that the noun phrase that immediately follows it is definitely identifiable...); sometimes after lhe, especially when referring to a body part, a family member, or a pet.; (precedes a familiar nickname or other term of address)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese o (compare Galician o), from Late Latin lo (compare Spanish lo) with loss of initial l, from earlier *illu, from Latin illum m, illud n, accusative singular forms of ille (“the”, “that”).

senses.gloss: partícula gramatical usada antes de substantivos ou palavras substantivadas; por geral indica uma coisa em particular

examples.text: Se o poeta sair, a festa acaba.

translations.de: Wenn der Dichter geht, ist die Party vorbei.
translations.en: If the poet leaves, the party's over.
translations.fr: Si le poète s'en va, la fête est finie.

examples.text: Qual é o preço do carro vermelho?

translations.de: Was kostet das rote Auto?
translations.en: What is the price of the red car?
translations.fr: Quel est le prix de la voiture rouge ?

examples.text: Dentro da jaula, o domador tomava café.

translations.de: Im Käfig trank der Tiertrainer Kaffee.
translations.en: Inside the cage, the animal trainer was drinking coffee.
translations.fr: À l'intérieur de la cage, le dresseur d'animaux buvait du café.

examples.text: Com ferramentas ruins o operário trabalha pior.

translations.de: Mit schlechtem Werkzeug leistet der Arbeiter schlechtere Arbeit.
translations.en: With poor tools, workers perform worse.
translations.fr: Avec de mauvais outils, le travailleur est moins performant.

more.definition: him, it (as a direct object; as an indirect object, see lhe; after prepositions, see ele)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese o (compare Galician o), from Late Latin lo (compare Spanish lo) with loss of initial l, from earlier *illu, from Latin illum m, illud n, accusative singular forms of ille (“the”, “that”).

examples.text: Eu sabia que eles estavam mentindo deliberadamente.

translations.de: Ich wusste, dass sie absichtlich logen.
translations.en: I knew they were lying deliberately.
translations.fr: Je savais qu'ils mentaient délibérément.

examples.text: Eu ajudo meu irmão sempre que possível.

translations.de: Ich helfe meinem Bruder, wann immer es mir möglich ist.
translations.en: I help my brother whenever I can.
translations.fr: J'aide mon frère autant que possible.

examples.text: O que você fez é incrível, parabéns!

translations.de: Was du geleistet hast, ist fantastisch. Herzlichen Glückwunsch!
translations.en: What you did is amazing, well done!
translations.fr: Ce que tu as fait est incroyable, bravo !

examples.text: Vou esperar até que voltes para mim.

translations.de: Ich warte, bis du zu mir zurückkommst.
translations.en: I'm going to wait until you come back to me.
translations.fr: Je vais attendre que tu reviennes vers moi.

more.definition: how (preceding adjectives) (indicates surprise, delight, or other strong feelings)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese que, from Latin quid (“what”) (usurping as well the roles of Latin quod), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷid, compare *kʷís. Cognate with English who.

examples.text: É exatamente isso que eu queria dizer.

translations.de: Das ist genau das, was ich sagen wollte.
translations.en: That is exactly what I wanted to say.
translations.fr: C'est exactement ce que je voulais dire.

examples.text: Acho que a prova vai ser fácil.

translations.de: Ich glaube, der Test wird einfach sein.
translations.en: I think the test will be easy.
translations.fr: Je pense que le test sera facile.

examples.text: Em que estação do ano estamos agora?

translations.de: In welcher Jahreszeit befinden wir uns gerade?
translations.en: Which season are we in right now?
translations.fr: Dans quelle saison sommes-nous actuellement ?

examples.text: Será que essa loucura um dia acaba?

translations.de: Wird dieser Wahnsinn jemals ein Ende finden?
translations.en: Will this madness ever end?
translations.fr: Cette folie finira-t-elle un jour ?

more.definition: that (connecting noun clause); that (introducing the result of the main clause); than (used in comparisons, to introduce the basis of comparison)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese que, from Latin quid (“what”) (usurping as well the roles of Latin quod), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷid, compare *kʷís. Cognate with English who.

senses.gloss: introduz orações subordinadas integrantes, consecutivas, causais, temporais, concessivas, finais e coordenadas explicativas

examples.text: Continuo sem saber do que se trata.

translations.de: Ich weiß noch immer nicht, worum es geht.
translations.en: I still don't know what it's about.
translations.fr: Je ne sais toujours pas de quoi il s'agit.

examples.text: Espero que isso não seja uma recusa.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, das ist keine Ablehnung.
translations.en: I hope this isn't a refusal.
translations.fr: J'espère que ce n'est pas un refus.

examples.text: Por que motivo estás fazendo essa pergunta?

translations.de: Warum stellen Sie diese Frage?
translations.en: Why are you asking that question?
translations.fr: Pourquoi poses-tu cette question ?

examples.text: E viu Deus que isso era bom.

translations.de: Und Gott sah, dass es gut war.
translations.en: And God saw that it was good.
translations.fr: Et Dieu vit que cela était bon.

more.definition: what (used to ask for a specification); what a (preceding nouns) (indicates surprise, delight, or other strong feelings)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese que, from Latin quid (“what”) (usurping as well the roles of Latin quod), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷid, compare *kʷís. Cognate with English who.

examples.text: Eu entrei sem que ninguém me visse.

translations.de: Ich bin hineingegangen, ohne dass mich jemand gesehen hat.
translations.en: I entered without anyone seeing me.
translations.fr: Je suis entré sans que personne ne me voie.

examples.text: Que ser é esse que chamamos Deus?

translations.de: Was ist dieses Wesen, das wir Gott nennen?
translations.en: What is this being we call God?
translations.fr: Quel est cet être que nous appelons Dieu ?

examples.text: Espero que ninguém descubra o que fizemos.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, es findet niemand heraus, was wir getan haben.
translations.en: I hope that nobody finds out what we did.
translations.fr: J'espère que personne ne découvre ce que nous avons fait.

examples.text: Pensei que ambas as frases fossem corretas.

translations.de: Ich dachte, dass beide Sätze richtig sind.
translations.en: I thought both sentences were correct.
translations.fr: Je pensais que les deux phrases étaient correctes.

more.definition: which; that; who (of those mentioned); whose; what thing
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese que, from Latin quid (“what”) (usurping as well the roles of Latin quod), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷid, compare *kʷís. Cognate with English who.

examples.text: Eu não trabalho mais. Agora, só estudo.

translations.de: Ich arbeite nicht mehr. Jetzt studiere ich nur noch.
translations.en: I don't work anymore. Now, I only study.
translations.fr: Je ne travaille plus. Maintenant, je me consacre uniquement aux études.

examples.text: Tudo pode mudar num piscar de olhos.

translations.de: Alles kann sich im Handumdrehen ändern.
translations.en: Everything can change in the blink of an eye.
translations.fr: Tout peut changer en un clin d’œil.

examples.text: Peguei um táxi, para não chegar tarde.

translations.de: Ich habe ein Taxi genommen, damit ich nicht zu spät ankomme.
translations.en: I took a taxi so I wouldn't arrive late.
translations.fr: 38 J'ai pris un taxi pour ne pas arriver en retard.

examples.text: Isso não é novo. Está acontecendo novamente.

translations.de: Das ist nichts Neues. Es passiert schon wieder.
translations.en: This is nothing new. It's happening again.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas nouveau. Cela se reproduit.

more.definition: not; don't; haven't (negates the meaning of the verb or adverb); used in sentences containing a negative pronoun as the object; see double negative; used to emphasise or reinforce (in the case that there is a previous unstressed adverb não, see above) sentences containing a negative pronoun as the subject or already containing não
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese non, from Latin nōn (“no”), from Old Latin noenum, from Proto-Indo-European *né (“not”) + *óynos (“one”).

senses.gloss: usado para negar verbos e adjetivos

examples.text: Eu não te deterei. Podes partir agora.

translations.de: Ich werde dich nicht aufhalten. Du kannst jetzt gehen.
translations.en: I won't stop you. You can leave now.
translations.fr: Je ne vous en empêcherai pas. Vous pouvez partir maintenant.

examples.text: O Natal cai num domingo este ano.

translations.de: Dieses Jahr fällt Weihnachten auf einen Sonntag.
translations.en: Christmas falls on Sunday this year.
translations.fr: Noël tombe un dimanche cette année.

examples.text: Os países não têm amigos — têm interesses.

translations.de: Länder haben keine Freunde – sie haben Interessen.
translations.en: Countries don't have friends—they have interests.
translations.fr: Les pays n’ont pas d’amis, ils ont des intérêts.

examples.text: É preciso não confundir alhos com bugalhos.

translations.de: Man darf Äpfel nicht mit Birnen verwechseln.
translations.en: It is important not to confuse apples with oranges.
translations.fr: Il ne faut pas confondre les pommes et les poires.

more.definition: no (used to show disagreement or negation); no (used to show agreement with a negative question)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese non, from Latin nōn (“no”), from Old Latin noenum, from Proto-Indo-European *né (“not”) + *óynos (“one”).

examples.text: O xadrez não é um jogo fácil.

translations.de: Schach ist kein einfaches Spiel.
translations.en: Chess is not an easy game.
translations.fr: Les échecs ne sont pas un jeu facile.

examples.text: Não, ele não está usando tua roupa.

translations.de: Nein, er trägt nicht Ihre Kleidung.
translations.en: No, he's not wearing your clothes.
translations.fr: Non, il ne porte pas tes vêtements.

examples.text: Essas coisas não são mencionadas na lei.

translations.de: Diese Dinge werden im Gesetz nicht erwähnt.
translations.en: Such things are not mentioned in the law.
translations.fr: Ces choses ne sont pas mentionnées dans la loi.

examples.text: Eu não sei como o Tom descobriu.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wie Tom das herausgefunden hat.
translations.en: I don't know how Tom found out.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas comment Tom l'a découvert.

more.definition: no (a negative answer)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese non, from Latin nōn (“no”), from Old Latin noenum, from Proto-Indo-European *né (“not”) + *óynos (“one”).

examples.text: Os animais são seres puros, naturais.

translations.de: Tiere sind reine, natürliche Wesen.
translations.en: Animals are pure, natural beings.
translations.fr: Les animaux sont des êtres purs et naturels.

more.definition: being (a living creature)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese ser, from Early Medieval Latin essere, from Latin esse. The forms sou (“I am”) and sois pl (“you are”) derive from a Vulgar Latin *sonō and *sutis. Along the way, the verb absorbed Old Galician-Portuguese seer < Latin sedēre (“sit”). The latter supplied the present subjunctive of modern ser, where /-ʒ-/ reflects Late Latin /-(d)j-/, as in seja < sedeat).

examples.text: Eu era feliz porque ela me amava.

translations.de: Ich war glücklich, weil sie mich liebte.
translations.en: I was happy because she loved me.
translations.fr: J'étais heureux parce qu'elle m'aimait.

examples.text: Meu irmão é tão trabalhador quanto eu.

translations.de: Mein Bruder ist genauso fleißig wie ich.
translations.en: My brother is just as hardworking as I am.
translations.fr: Mon frère est tout aussi travailleur que moi.

examples.text: A árvore cresceu demais, deve ser podada.

translations.de: Der Baum ist zu groß geworden, er muss beschnitten werden.
translations.en: The tree has grown too big, it must be pruned.
translations.fr: L'arbre est devenu trop grand, il faut le tailler.

examples.text: A guerra é fratricídio insano e imperdoável.

translations.de: Kriege sind wahnsinnige und unverzeihliche Brudermorde.
translations.en: The war is insane and unforgivable fratricide.
translations.fr: La guerre est un acte de folie et un fratricide impardonnable.

more.definition: to be (to have the given quality), especially a quality that is intrinsic or not expected to change, contrasting with estar which denotes a temporary quality; to be (to be an example or type of, or the same as); to be; forms the passive voice
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese ser, from Early Medieval Latin essere, from Latin esse. The forms sou (“I am”) and sois pl (“you are”) derive from a Vulgar Latin *sonō and *sutis. Along the way, the verb absorbed Old Galician-Portuguese seer < Latin sedēre (“sit”). The latter supplied the present subjunctive of modern ser, where /-ʒ-/ reflects Late Latin /-(d)j-/, as in seja < sedeat).

senses.gloss: ter como característica ou propriedade de si mesmo

examples.text: Não estou com fome. Acabei de almoçar.

translations.de: Ich habe keinen Hunger. Ich habe gerade zu Mittag gegessen.
translations.en: I'm not hungry. I just had lunch.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas faim. Je viens de déjeuner.

examples.text: Tenho noventa e três anos de idade.

translations.de: Ich bin dreiundneunzig Jahre alt.
translations.en: I am ninety-three years old.
translations.fr: J'ai quatre-vingt-treize ans.

examples.text: Depois de acordar, eu geralmente tomo banho...

translations.de: Nach dem Aufwachen dusche ich normalerweise...
translations.en: After waking up, I usually take a shower...
translations.fr: Après m'être réveillé, je prends généralement une douche...

examples.text: Alguém pegou dinheiro de minha carteira hoje?

translations.de: Hat heute jemand Geld aus meiner Brieftasche genommen?
translations.en: Did someone take money from my wallet today?
translations.fr: Quelqu'un a-t-il pris de l'argent dans mon portefeuille aujourd'hui ?

more.definition: of (in relation to); of (forms compounds; often untranslated); of; about (on the subject of)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese de, from Latin dē, from Proto-Italic *dē, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₁, from *de + *-h₁. Cognate with Galician de.

senses.gloss: estabelece uma ligação entre duas palavras, (geralmente uma relação de subordinação), podendo expressar

examples.text: Hoje eu vi uma cobra no jardim.

translations.de: Heute habe ich eine Schlange im Garten gesehen.
translations.en: Today I saw a snake in the garden.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, j'ai vu un serpent dans le jardin.

examples.text: A chuva chove mansamente como um sono.

translations.de: Der Regen fällt sanft wie ein Schlaf.
translations.en: The rain falls gently like sleep.
translations.fr: La pluie tombe doucement comme un sommeil.

examples.text: Eu tenho uma televisão em meu quarto.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Fernseher in meinem Zimmer.
translations.en: I have a television in my room.
translations.fr: J'ai une télévision dans ma chambre.

examples.text: Esse complexo esportivo tem uma piscina olímpica.

translations.de: Dieser Sportkomplex verfügt über ein olympisches Schwimmbecken.
translations.en: This sports complex has an Olympic-size swimming pool.
translations.fr: Ce complexe sportif dispose d'une piscine olympique.

more.definition: a, an; some; a few (a small number of); a bit of
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ũu (“one; a”), from Latin ūnum (“one”), from Old Latin oinos, from Proto-Italic *oinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). Doublet of uno.

examples.text: Agora estou lendo um livro muito bom.

translations.de: Ich lese gerade ein sehr gutes Buch.
translations.en: I am currently reading a very good book.
translations.fr: Je suis en train de lire un très bon livre.

examples.text: Tatoeba é um dicionário multilíngue e interativo.

translations.de: Tatoeba ist ein mehrsprachiges und interaktives Wörterbuch.
translations.en: Tatoeba is a multilingual and interactive dictionary.
translations.fr: Tatoeba est un dictionnaire multilingue et interactif.

examples.text: O futebol é um esporte de equipe.

translations.de: Fußball ist ein Mannschaftssport.
translations.en: Soccer is a team sport.
translations.fr: Le football est un sport d'équipe.

examples.text: Aquilo é um touro ou um boi?

translations.de: Ist das ein Stier oder ein Ochse?
translations.en: Is that a bull or an ox?
translations.fr: Est-ce un taureau ou un bœuf ?

more.definition: the figure or digit "1": one
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ũu (“one; a”), from Latin ūnum (“one”), from Old Latin oinos, from Proto-Italic *oinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). Doublet of uno.

examples.text: O tio dele tinha uma voz linda.

translations.de: Sein Onkel hatte eine wunderschöne Stimme.
translations.en: His uncle had a beautiful voice.
translations.fr: Son oncle avait une voix magnifique.

examples.text: O homem deu um passo para trás.

translations.de: Der Mann wich einen Schritt zurück.
translations.en: The man took a step back.
translations.fr: L'homme recula d'un pas.

examples.text: Temos uma torneira especial para água potável.

translations.de: Wir haben einen speziellen Wasserhahn für Trinkwasser.
translations.en: We have a special tap for drinking water.
translations.fr: Nous avons un robinet spécial pour l'eau potable.

examples.text: A verdade é um segredo bem guardado.

translations.de: Die Wahrheit ist ein gut gehütetes Geheimnis.
translations.en: The truth is a well-kept secret.
translations.fr: La vérité est un secret bien gardé.

more.definition: one
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ũu (“one; a”), from Latin ūnum (“one”), from Old Latin oinos, from Proto-Italic *oinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). Doublet of uno.

senses.gloss: representa a cardinalidade de um conjunto que não seja vazio e que contenha o menor número inteiro de elementos possíveis; representado pelo símbolo 1 (algarismos indo-arábicos) ou I (algarismos romanos); seu feminino é uma

examples.text: Estou só à espera de um amigo.

translations.de: Ich warte gerade auf einen Freund.
translations.en: I'm just waiting for a friend.
translations.fr: J'attends juste un ami.

examples.text: Nada se ensina corretamente sem um exemplo.

translations.de: Nichts wird ohne Beispiel richtig gelehrt.
translations.en: Nothing is taught correctly without an example.
translations.fr: Rien n'est enseigné correctement sans un exemple.

examples.text: Meu filho é um professor de inglês.

translations.de: Mein Sohn ist Englischlehrer.
translations.en: My son is an English teacher.
translations.fr: Mon fils est professeur d'anglais.

examples.text: Ela se apaixonou por um certo príncipe.

translations.de: Sie hat sich in einen bestimmten Prinzen verliebt.
translations.en: She fell in love with a certain prince.
translations.fr: Elle est tombée amoureuse d'un certain prince.

more.definition: a person; one; someone; element(s) of a previously mentioned class: one; some (in the plural)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ũu (“one; a”), from Latin ūnum (“one”), from Old Latin oinos, from Proto-Italic *oinos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos (“one”). Doublet of uno.

examples.text: Alegre ou triste, você é sempre linda.

translations.de: Ob glücklich oder traurig, du bist immer schön.
translations.en: Whether happy or sad, you are always beautiful.
translations.fr: Que tu sois heureuse ou triste, tu es toujours belle.

examples.text: Eu não preciso da ajuda de vocês.

translations.de: Ich brauche Ihre Hilfe nicht.
translations.en: I don't need your help.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas besoin de votre aide.

examples.text: Até quanto você sabe contar em turco?

translations.de: Wie weit können Sie auf Türkisch zählen?
translations.en: How far can you count in Turkish?
translations.fr: Jusqu'où savez-vous compter en turc ?

examples.text: Acho que você deveria assistir esse filme.

translations.de: Ich finde, diesen Film solltest du sehen.
translations.en: I think that you should watch this movie.
translations.fr: Je pense que tu devrais regarder ce film.

more.definition: second-person singular personal pronoun, formal or informal in Brazil, formal or semi-formal in Portugal; you; indefinite pronoun; you, one
more.etymology: Syncope of vosmecê, elision of vossemecê, contraction of Old Galician-Portuguese vossa mercee (literally “your mercy”) (today's mercê) from Latin vostram + mercēdem. Compare with Spanish usted (from vuestra merced (literally “your mercy”)) and Catalan vostè.

senses.gloss: aquele a quem se fala ou escreve

examples.text: Fui até ele e o encontrei chorando.

translations.de: Ich ging zu ihm und fand ihn weinend.
translations.en: I went to him and found him crying.
translations.fr: Je suis allé vers lui et je l'ai trouvé en train de pleurer.

examples.text: Existe alguma diferença entre cultura e educação?

translations.de: Gibt es einen Unterschied zwischen Kultur und Bildung?
translations.en: Is there any difference between culture and education?
translations.fr: Y a-t-il une différence entre culture et éducation ?

examples.text: O mar é muito grande e profundo.

translations.de: Das Meer ist sehr groß und tief.
translations.en: The sea is very large and deep.
translations.fr: La mer est très grande et profonde.

examples.text: Trinta meses são dois anos e meio.

translations.de: Dreißig Monate sind zweieinhalb Jahre.
translations.en: Thirty months is two and a half years.
translations.fr: Trente mois, c'est deux ans et demi.

more.definition: and (connects two clauses indicating that the events occurred together, one after the other or without any special implication); and (connects the last and penultimate elements in a list); what about
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese e, from Latin et.

senses.gloss: conjunção coordenativa aditiva usada para unir orações ou termos de mesma natureza gramatical

examples.text: Ela tem cabelos castanhos e covinhas encantadoras.

translations.de: Sie hat braunes Haar und bezaubernde Grübchen.
translations.en: She has brown hair and charming dimples.
translations.fr: Elle a les cheveux bruns et de charmantes fossettes.

examples.text: Hoje é sábado e meu time jogará.

translations.de: Heute ist Samstag und meine Mannschaft spielt.
translations.en: Today is Saturday, and my team is going to play.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, c'est samedi et mon équipe va jouer.

examples.text: Experimentamos a vida como sensações e sentimentos.

translations.de: Wir erleben das Leben als Empfindungen und Gefühle.
translations.en: We experience life as sensations and feelings.
translations.fr: Nous vivons la vie sous forme de sensations et de sentiments.

examples.text: Inferno e céu são criações da mente.

translations.de: Himmel und Hölle sind Schöpfungen des Geistes.
translations.en: Hell and heaven are mental creations.
translations.fr: L’enfer et le paradis sont des impressions mentales.

more.definition: and, conjunction; abbreviation of este (“east”): E
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese e, from Latin et.

examples.text: Se eu fosse rico, eu te ajudaria.

translations.de: Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich dir helfen.
translations.en: If I were rich, I would help you.
translations.fr: Si j'étais riche, je t'aiderais.

examples.text: Visto que o desejas, eu o farei.

translations.de: Da Sie es wünschen, werde ich es tun.
translations.en: Since you wish it, I will do it.
translations.fr: Puisque tu le souhaites, je le ferai.

examples.text: Não é isso o que eu quero.

translations.de: Das ist nicht das, was ich will.
translations.en: That's not what I want.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas ce que je veux.

translations.en: I didn't know where it came from.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas d'où ça venait.

more.definition: that (the thing near you; the thing mentioned that concerns you); this (the thing near me; the thing mentioned that concerns me)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese esso, from Latin ipsum, neuter of ipse (“itself”).

senses.gloss: essa coisa ou esse assunto; essas coisas; esses assuntos

examples.text: A vida é o que fazemos dela.

translations.de: Das Leben ist, was wir daraus machen.
translations.en: Life is what we make of it.
translations.fr: La vie est ce que nous en faisons.

examples.text: O Jean faz música, mas não canta.

translations.de: Johannes macht Musik, singt aber nicht.
translations.en: John makes music, but doesn't sing.
translations.fr: Jean fait de la musique, mais ne chante pas.

examples.text: Não tenho nada que fazer esta tarde.

translations.de: Ich habe heute Nachmittag nichts zu tun.
translations.en: I have nothing to do this afternoon.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien à faire cet après-midi.

examples.text: Estava fazendo bastante frio ontem de manhã.

translations.de: Gestern Morgen war es sehr kalt.
translations.en: It was very cold yesterday morning.
translations.fr: Il faisait très froid hier matin.

more.definition: to create; to produce; to do; to execute; to perform; to cause to
idioms: fazer a cama e deitar-se nela
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese fazer. Compare Galician facer, Spanish hacer, Italian fare.

examples.text: Não consigo imaginar minha vida sem Tatoeba.

translations.de: Ich kann mir mein Leben ohne Tatoeba nicht vorstellen.
translations.en: I can't imagine my life without Tatoeba.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas imaginer ma vie sans Tatoeba.

examples.text: O meu pai gosta de café forte.

translations.de: Mein Vater mag starken Kaffee.
translations.en: My father likes strong coffee.
translations.fr: Mon père aime le café fort.

examples.text: Todos os meus livros estão aqui.

translations.de: Alle meine Bücher sind hier.
translations.en: All my books are here.
translations.fr: Tous mes livres sont ici.

examples.text: Jamais te esquecerei, amor de minha vida!

translations.de: Ich werde dich nie vergessen, Liebe meines Lebens!
translations.en: I will never forget you, the love of my life!
translations.fr: Je ne t'oublierai jamais, amour de ma vie !

more.definition: my (belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of me)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese meu, from Latin meus, from Proto-Italic *meos.

examples.text: Eu gosto do meu bife mal passado.

translations.de: Ich mag mein Steak leicht angebraten.
translations.en: I like my steak rare.
translations.fr: J'aime mon bifteck saignant.

examples.text: O nome do meu filho é Tom.

translations.de: Der Name meines Sohnes ist Tom.
translations.en: My son's name is Tom.
translations.fr: Le nom de mon fils est Tom.

examples.text: O meu pai não está em casa.

translations.de: Papa ist nicht zu Hause.
translations.en: My father isn't at home.
translations.fr: Mon père n’est pas à la maison.

examples.text: Essa palavra não está no meu dicionário.

translations.de: Dieses Wort ist nicht in meinem Wörterbuch.
translations.en: That word isn't in my dictionary.
translations.fr: Ce mot n'est pas dans mon dictionnaire.

more.definition: hey; oi (used vocatively to draw someone’s attention); whoa (used to express surprise); dude
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese meu, from Latin meus, from Proto-Italic *meos.

examples.text: A voz de minha mãe é inconfundível.

translations.de: Die Stimme meiner Mutter ist unverkennbar.
translations.en: My mother's voice is unmistakable.
translations.fr: La voix de ma mère est unique.

examples.text: Todo domingo é santo, meu querido primo.

translations.de: Jeder Sonntag ist heilig, mein lieber Vetter.
translations.en: Every Sunday is holy, my dear cousin.
translations.fr: Chaque dimanche est saint, mon cher cousin.

examples.text: Irei quando tiver terminado minhas tarefas aqui.

translations.de: Ich werde gehen, wenn ich meine Pflichten hier erledigt habe.
translations.en: I shall go when I shall have completed my chores here.
translations.fr: J'irai quand j'aurai terminé mes corvées ici.

examples.text: Os meus pais não são estritos comigo.

translations.de: Meine Eltern sind nicht streng zu mir.
translations.en: My parents are not strict with me.
translations.fr: Mes deux parents ne sont pas stricts avec moi.

more.definition: mine (used substantively, with an implied noun)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese meu, from Latin meus, from Proto-Italic *meos.

examples.text: Recebi a mensagem dela no meu celular.

translations.de: Ich habe ihre Nachricht auf meinem Handy erhalten.
translations.en: I got her message on my phone.
translations.fr: J'ai reçu son message sur mon téléphone.

examples.text: Quero beijar-te as mãos, minha querida.

translations.de: Ich möchte deine Hände küssen, meine Liebe.
translations.en: I want to kiss your hands, my dear.
translations.fr: Je veux embrasser tes mains, mon amour.

examples.text: Aquela foi a viagem dos meus sonhos.

translations.de: Das war die Reise meiner Träume.
translations.en: That was the trip of my dreams.
translations.fr: C'était le voyage de mes rêves.

examples.text: Ainda encontro em minhas frases muitos erros.

translations.de: Ich finde immer noch viele Fehler in meinen Sätzen.
translations.en: I still find many mistakes in my sentences.
translations.fr: Je trouve encore beaucoup d'erreurs dans mes phrases.

more.definition: mine (used predicatively); mine (used absolutely, set off from the sentence)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese meu, from Latin meus, from Proto-Italic *meos.

senses.gloss: de posse da primeira pessoa do singular (eu); pertencente a mim

examples.text: Hoje aprendi cinco novas palavras em turco.

translations.de: Heute habe ich fünf neue türkische Wörter gelernt.
translations.en: Today I learned five new words in Turkish.
translations.fr: Aujourd'hui, j'ai appris cinq nouveaux mots en turc.

examples.text: A caixa está em cima da mesa.

translations.de: Die Kiste steht auf dem Tisch.
translations.en: The box is on the table.
translations.fr: La boîte est sur la table.

examples.text: A língua latina está viva em Tatoeba.

translations.de: Die lateinische Sprache ist in Tatoeba lebendig.
translations.en: The Latin language is alive on Tatoeba.
translations.fr: La langue latine est vivante à Tatoeba.

examples.text: Muitas pessoas usam Toki Pona em Tatoeba.

translations.de: Viele Leute benutzen Toki Pona in Tatoeba.
translations.en: Many people use Toki Pona in Tatoeba.
translations.fr: Beaucoup de gens utilisent le toki pona à Tatoeba.

more.definition: in; inside; within (contained by); on; on top of (located just above the surface of); in; at (located in a location)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese en, from Latin in (“in”), from Proto-Italic *en, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁én (“in”). Doublet of in.

more.definition: knowledge; lore (intellectual understanding)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese saber, from Latin sapere (“taste, know”). The verb’s first-person singular conjugation reflects an original */ˈsajo/, in common with other Romance languages, of uncertain origin. The present subjunctive forms show consonant metathesis: sapiām > */ˈsajpa/ > Portuguese saiba.

examples.text: É útil saber falar Francês em Paris.

translations.de: Es ist nützlich zu wissen, wie man in Paris Französisch spricht.
translations.en: It is useful to know how to speak French in Paris.
translations.fr: Il est utile de savoir parler français à Paris.

examples.text: Eu sei que devo terminar o trabalho.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass ich die Arbeit zu Ende bringen muss.
translations.en: I know I must finish the job.
translations.fr: Je sais que je dois finir le travail.

examples.text: Eu não sabia que ela me amava.

translations.de: Ich wusste nicht, dass sie mich liebt.
translations.en: I didn't know that she loved me.
translations.fr: Je ne savais pas qu'elle m'aimait.

examples.text: Nós sabemos que ela nasceu no Canadá.

translations.de: Wir wissen, dass sie in Kanada geboren wurde.
translations.en: We know that she was born in Canada.
translations.fr: Nous savons qu'elle est née au Canada.

more.definition: to be aware, to know; to be aware of a value or piece of information; to know how
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese saber, from Latin sapere (“taste, know”). The verb’s first-person singular conjugation reflects an original */ˈsajo/, in common with other Romance languages, of uncertain origin. The present subjunctive forms show consonant metathesis: sapiām > */ˈsajpa/ > Portuguese saiba.

senses.gloss: conhecer, ter conhecimento de, estar informado sobre, ser sabedor

examples.text: Somos padrões no fluxo eterno do cosmos.

translations.de: Wir sind Muster im ewigen Fluss des Kosmos.
translations.en: We are patterns in the eternal flow of the cosmos.
translations.fr: Nous sommes des motifs dans le flux éternel du cosmos.

examples.text: Qual é a forma escrita do silêncio?

translations.de: Wie sieht die schriftliche Form der Stille aus?
translations.en: What is the written form of silence?
translations.fr: Quelle est la forme écrite du silence ?

examples.text: O final do filme é muito triste.

translations.de: Das Ende des Films ist sehr traurig.
translations.en: The ending of the movie is very sad.
translations.fr: La fin du film est très triste.

examples.text: Esse doutor quer me matar do coração.

translations.de: Dieser Arzt möchte bei mir einen Herzinfarkt verursachen.
translations.en: This doctor wants to give me a heart attack.
translations.fr: Ce médecin veut me donner une crise cardiaque.

more.definition: contraction of de + o, literally “of the, from the, -'s (masculine singular)”
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese do, from de (“of, from”) + o (“the”). Akin to Galician do, Italian and Spanish del, French du and Sicilian dû ~ dô.

examples.text: Atenas me encantou, pelo menos a cidade.

translations.de: Athen hat mich verzaubert, zumindest die Stadt selbst.
translations.en: Athens enchanted me, at least the city itself.
translations.fr: Athènes m'a enchantée, du moins la ville elle-même.

examples.text: Estou me sentindo melhor agora de manhã.

translations.de: Jetzt morgens geht es mir besser.
translations.en: I feel better now in the morning.
translations.fr: Je me sens mieux maintenant le matin.

examples.text: Que mãozinha fria! Permita-me aquecê-la.

translations.de: Was für eine kalte, kleine Hand! Erlauben Sie mir, sie aufzuwärmen.
translations.en: What a cold little hand! Allow me to warm it up.
translations.fr: Quelle petite main froide ! Permettez-moi de la réchauffer.

examples.text: Tu logo me esqueceste, ó mulher inconstante!

translations.de: Du hast mich bald vergessen, du wankelmütiges Weib!
translations.en: You soon forgot me, you fickle woman!
translations.fr: Tu m'as vite oublié, ô femme volage !

more.definition: first-person singular objective direct personal pronoun; me; first-person singular objective indirect personal pronoun; (to) me; first-person singular reflexive pronoun; myself
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese me, from Latin mē (accusative of ego), from Proto-Indo-European *(e)me-. As an objective indirect pronoun, possibly in part from Latin mihi (dative of ego), through a Vulgar Latin *mi.

senses.gloss: pronome pessoal oblíquo átono da primeira pessoa do singular, usado em complementos direto do verbo:

examples.text: Eu sou bem forte, porém hoje vou chorar.

translations.de: Ich bin sehr stark, aber heute werde ich weinen.
translations.en: I'm very strong, but today I'm going to cry.
translations.fr: Je suis très fort, mais aujourd'hui je vais pleurer.

examples.text: Estou com frio apesar de estar bem agasalhado.

translations.de: Mir ist kalt, obwohl ich warm angezogen bin.
translations.en: I'm cold despite being well dressed.
translations.fr: J'ai froid même si je suis bien habillé.

examples.text: O pranto é vizinho bem próximo da alegria.

translations.de: Das Weinen ist ein sehr enger Nachbar der Freude.
translations.en: Weeping is a very close neighbour of joy.
translations.fr: Les pleurs sont un voisin très proche de la joie.

examples.text: Marina canta bem. Ela tem uma bela voz.

translations.de: Marina singt gut. Sie hat eine schöne Stimme.
translations.en: Marina sings well. She has a beautiful voice.
translations.fr: Marina chante bien. Elle a une belle voix.

more.definition: well; accurately; competently; well; fairly; rather (to a significant degree); very; really (to a high degree)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ben, from Latin bene (“well”).

examples.text: Saúde, bem-estar — felicidade. Enfermidade, mal-estar — infelicidade.

translations.de: Gesundheit, Wohlbefinden – Glück. Krankheit, Unwohlsein – Unglück.
translations.en: Health, well-being — happiness. Illness, malaise — unhappiness.
translations.fr: Santé, bien-être — bonheur. Maladie, inconfort — malheur.

examples.text: Eu falei bem devagar, para que ela entendesse.

translations.de: Ich sprach sehr langsam, damit sie mich verstehen würde.
translations.en: I spoke very slowly so that she would understand.
translations.fr: J'ai parlé très lentement pour qu'elle comprenne.

examples.text: Ele sabe boiar, mas não nada muito bem.

translations.de: Er kann sich über Wasser halten, schwimmt aber nicht besonders gut.
translations.en: He can float, but he isn't much of a swimmer.
translations.fr: Il sait flotter, mais il ne nage pas très bien.

examples.text: Coroa e pedra preciosa são coisas bem diferentes.

translations.de: Eine Krone und ein Edelstein sind zwei ganz verschiedene Dinge.
translations.en: A crown and a precious stone are very different things.
translations.fr: Une couronne et une pierre précieuse sont deux choses très différentes.

more.definition: Used to express approval.; well (used to introduce a new sentence, idea or line of thought)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ben, from Latin bene (“well”).

examples.text: Tenho muitos amigos que falam bem português.

translations.de: Ich habe viele Freunde, die gut Portugiesisch sprechen.
translations.en: I have a lot of friends that can speak Portuguese well.
translations.fr: J'ai beaucoup d'amis qui peuvent bien parler le portugais.

examples.text: Eu espero que o Tom esteja bem.

translations.de: Ich hoffe, Tom geht es gut.
translations.en: I hope Tom is all right.
translations.fr: J'espère que Tom va bien.

examples.text: Conheço alguém que fala francês muito bem.

translations.de: Ich kenne jemanden, der sehr gut Französisch spricht.
translations.en: I know someone who speaks French very well.
translations.fr: Je connais quelqu'un qui parle très bien français.

examples.text: Harmonia entre os pais — bem-estar dos filhos.

translations.de: Harmonie zwischen den Eltern – das Wohlbefinden der Kinder.
translations.en: Harmony between parents — children's well-being.
translations.fr: L'harmonie entre les parents — le bien-être des enfants.

more.definition: good (the ensemble of forces that conspire for good, as opposed to evil); good; well-being; a good deed
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese ben, from Latin bene (“well”).

examples.text: A mesa é pequena, mas é pesada.

translations.de: Der Tisch ist klein aber schwer.
translations.en: The table is small but heavy.
translations.fr: La table est petite mais lourde.

examples.text: Ama a verdade, mas perdoa o erro.

translations.de: Liebe die Wahrheit, doch verzeihe den Irrtum.
translations.en: Love truth, but pardon error.
translations.fr: Aime la vérité, mais pardonne l'erreur.

examples.text: Ele é rico, mas não é feliz.

translations.de: Er ist reich, aber nicht glücklich.
translations.en: He's rich, but he isn't happy.
translations.fr: Il est riche mais il n'est pas heureux.

examples.text: Jim não é advogado, mas sim médico.

translations.de: Jim ist nicht Anwalt, sondern Arzt.
translations.en: Jim's not a lawyer. He's a doctor.
translations.fr: Jim n'est pas avocat mais médecin.

more.definition: emphasises a previous clause, adverb or adjective; really; and how
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese mas, from Latin magis (“more”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“great”). Doublet of mais.

examples.text: Ele cria poucas frases, mas faz muitas traduções.

translations.de: Er verfasst wenige Sätze, fertigt aber viele Übersetzungen an.
translations.en: He creates very few sentences, but does many translations.
translations.fr: Il crée peu de phrases, mais fait beaucoup de traductions.

examples.text: A justiça é cega, mas não é tola.

translations.de: Die Gerechtigkeit ist blind, aber sie ist nicht dumm.
translations.en: Justice is blind, but it is not foolish.
translations.fr: La justice est aveugle, mais elle n’est pas stupide.

examples.text: Ela deixa muitas saudades, mas também muitas belezas.

translations.de: Sie hinterlässt viel Nostalgie, aber auch viel Schönheit.
translations.en: She leaves behind a lot of nostalgia, but also a lot of beauty.
translations.fr: Elle laisse derrière elle beaucoup de nostalgie, mais aussi beaucoup de beauté.

examples.text: Religiões há muitas, mas espiritualidade há uma só.

translations.de: Es gibt viele Religionen, aber nur eine Spiritualität.
translations.en: There are many religions, but there is only one spirituality.
translations.fr: Il existe de nombreuses religions, mais il n’existe qu’une seule spiritualité.

more.definition: but (introduces a clause that contradicts the implications of the previous clause); but (introduces the correct information for something that was denied in the previous clause); but ... really; of course; no wonder (introduces the cause of the previous clause, with the implication that the result was expected given this cause)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese mas, from Latin magis (“more”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“great”). Doublet of mais.

senses.gloss: conjunção coordenativa adversativa, indicando essencialmente contradição ou restrição quanto às ideias, nos casos enumerados adiante: (re)estabelecer a verdade de algo

examples.text: Os cães ladram, mas a caravana passa.

translations.de: Die Hunde bellen, aber die Karawane zieht weiter.
translations.en: The dogs bark, but the caravan moves on.
translations.fr: Les chiens aboient, mais la caravane passe.

examples.text: A porta estava aberta, mas agora está fechada.

translations.de: Die Tür war offen, aber jetzt ist sie geschlossen.
translations.en: The door was open, but now it is closed.
translations.fr: La porte était ouverte, mais elle est désormais fermée.

examples.text: Os esquimós usam caiaques, mas não sabem esquiar.

translations.de: Die Inuit benutzen Kajaks, aber sie können nicht Ski fahren.
translations.en: Inuit use kayaks, but they don't know how to ski.
translations.fr: Les Inuits utilisent des kayaks, mais ils ne savent pas skier.

examples.text: Ele nasceu pobre, mas morreu rico.

translations.de: Er wurde arm geboren, starb aber reich.
translations.en: He was born poor, but he died rich.
translations.fr: Il est né pauvre, mais il est mort riche.

more.definition: but (an instance of proclaiming an exception)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese mas, from Latin magis (“more”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *meǵh₂- (“great”). Doublet of mais.
Do português antigo dizer, dicer (“idem”), formado do infinitivo latino dicere, do verbo dico (“idem”).

examples.text: Eu te digo isto porque te amo.

translations.de: Ich sage dir das, weil ich dich liebe.
translations.en: I tell you this because I love you.
translations.fr: Je te dis ça parce que je t'aime.

examples.text: Tom disse que preferiria ficar em casa.

translations.de: Tom sagte, er wolle lieber zu Hause bleiben.
translations.en: Tom said he'd prefer to stay at home.
translations.fr: Tom a dit qu’il préférerait rester à la maison.

examples.text: Como se diz XXX na sua língua?

translations.de: Wie sagt man XXX in deiner Sprache?
translations.en: How do you say XXX in your language?
translations.fr: Comment dit-on XXX dans ta langue ?

examples.text: Eu não ligo para o que dizem.

translations.de: Ich achte nicht darauf, was sie sagen.
translations.en: I don't care about what they say.
translations.fr: Je ne fais pas attention à ce qu'ils disent.

more.definition: to speak; to pronounce; to utter; to say; to tell; to say (to communicate information to someone); to say (to indicate a given fact)
idioms: dizer cobras e lagartos de alguém
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese dizer, from Latin dīcere, from Proto-Italic *deikō, from Proto-Indo-European *déyḱeti (“to show, point out”). Compare Galician dicir.

examples.text: O mundo inteiro está enamorado do Brasil.

translations.de: Die ganze Welt ist in Brasilien verliebt.
translations.en: The whole world is in love with Brazil.
translations.fr: Le monde entier est amoureux du Brésil.

examples.text: Onde está a minha certidão de nascimento?

translations.de: Wo ist meine Geburtsurkunde?
translations.en: Where's my birth certificate?
translations.fr: Où est mon acte de naissance ?

examples.text: O que você está vendo nessa imagem?

translations.de: Was siehst du auf diesem Bild?
translations.en: What do you see in this image?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu vois dans cette image ?

examples.text: O Tom está escrevendo para uma amiga.

translations.de: Tom schreibt einer Freundin.
translations.en: Tom is writing to a friend.
translations.fr: Tom écrit à une amie.

examples.text: Às vezes, ao querer punir o mal, o justo se converte em malfeitor.

translations.de: Manchmal wird der Gerechte, wenn er das Böse bestrafen will, selbst zum Übeltäter.
translations.en: Sometimes, in seeking to punish evil, the righteous become evildoers themselves.
translations.fr: Parfois, en voulant punir le mal, les justes deviennent des malfaiteurs.

more.definition: desire, will
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese querer, from Latin quaerere (“seek, look for, desire”). Compare Galician querer.

examples.text: Eu não quero mais viver em Boston.

translations.de: Ich möchte nicht mehr in Boston wohnen.
translations.en: I no longer want to live in Boston.
translations.fr: Je ne veux plus vivre à Boston.

examples.text: A menina quis satisfazer a irmãzinha.

translations.de: Das Mädchen wollte ihrer kleinen Schwester eine Freude machen.
translations.en: The girl wanted to please her little sister.
translations.fr: La jeune fille voulait faire plaisir à sa petite sœur.

examples.text: Você pode dar o livro a quem quiser.

translations.de: Du kannst das Buch geben, wem du willst.
translations.en: You can give the book to whoever you want.
translations.fr: Vous pouvez offrir le livre à qui vous voulez.

examples.text: Não queira ser o que você não é.

translations.de: Versuchen Sie nicht, etwas zu sein, was Sie nicht sind.
translations.en: Don't try to be what you're not.
translations.fr: Ne cherchez pas à être ce que vous n'êtes pas.

more.definition: to want; to wish; to desire; to want; to want to (to feel the need to do something)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese querer, from Latin quaerere (“seek, look for, desire”). Compare Galician querer.

examples.text: O objetivo da política depende dos políticos.

translations.de: Das Ziel der Politik hängt von den Politikern ab.
translations.en: The goal of politics depends on the politicians.
translations.fr: Le but de la politique dépend des politiciens.

examples.text: Cinema é arte, sonho, imitação da vida.

translations.de: Kino ist Kunst, Traum, Nachahmung des Lebens.
translations.en: Cinema is art, dream, imitation of life.
translations.fr: Le cinéma est un art, un rêve, une imitation de la vie.

examples.text: A beleza é a canção da vida.

translations.de: Schönheit ist das Lied des Lebens.
translations.en: Beauty is the song of life.
translations.fr: La beauté est le chant de la vie.

examples.text: Mary fez vinte traduções da mesma frase.

translations.de: Maria hat zwanzig Übersetzungen desselben Satzes angefertigt.
translations.en: Mary made twenty translations of the same sentence.
translations.fr: Marie a fait vingt traductions de la même phrase.

more.definition: contraction of de + a, literally “of/from the (feminine singular)”: feminine singular of do
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese da, from de (“of”) + a (“feminine definite article”). Compare Sicilian dâ.

examples.text: Encontrei no armário uma ninhada de ratinhos.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Wurf Babymäuse im Schrank gefunden.
translations.en: I found a nest of baby mice in the closet.
translations.fr: J'ai trouvé une portée de bébés souris dans le placard.

examples.text: Nosso professor nos ensina principalmente a trabalhar.

translations.de: Unser Lehrer bringt uns hauptsächlich das Arbeiten bei.
translations.en: Our teacher mainly teaches us how to work.
translations.fr: Notre professeur nous apprend principalement à travailler.

examples.text: Há mais portas ou janelas no mundo?

translations.fr: Sais-tu comment faire ceci ?

translations.fr: Elle est aussi jeune que moi.

translations.de: Sei nicht faul! Sieh dir an, wie fleißig dein Bruder ist!

translations.fr: Ne sois pas paresseux ! Regarde comme ton frère travaille dur !

examples.text: Resolvam o problema e expliquem como encontraram a solução.

translations.fr: Résolvez le problème et expliquez comment vous avez trouvé la solution.

translations.fr: Rien n'existe en dehors de Toi.

examples.text: Você nunca vai saber como sinto a sua falta.

translations.fr: Tu ne sauras jamais à quel point tu me manques.

translations.en: Learning languages is like a workout for the brain.

examples.text: Quem só faz o bem pode viver como quiser.

translations.fr: Celui qui ne fait que du bien peut vivre comme il l'entend.

more.definition: what? sorry? pardon? (used as a request for someone to repeat something not heard or understood clearly)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese como (“how; in what way”), from Latin cōmō̆, a non-literary form of quōmodo.

examples.text: A senhorita é modesta como uma violeta.

translations.fr: Apprenez-le par cœur comme si c'était le Notre Père.

translations.fr: Des larmes comme celles-là ne peuvent venir que du cœur.

examples.text: Eu não sei como Tom descobriu.

examples.text: O rosto dele ficou branco como papel.

translations.de: Sein Gesicht wurde kreidebleich.
translations.en: His face turned as white as a sheet.
translations.fr: Son visage devint blanc comme du papier.

examples.text: Me conte como você resolveu o problema.

translations.fr: Dis-moi comment tu as résolu le problème.

examples.text: Ninguém me conhece como você me conhece.

translations.fr: Personne ne me connaît autant que toi.

examples.text: Quioto não é tão grande como Osaca.

translations.en: Kyoto is not as large as Osaka.
translations.fr: Kyoto n'est pas aussi grand qu'Osaka.

more.etymology: Do latim quomodo (qual modo), por meio da forma reduzida quomo.

examples.text: A aula de hoje foi muito proveitosa.

translations.de: Der heutige Unterricht war sehr produktiv.
translations.en: Today's class was very productive.
translations.fr: Le cours d'aujourd'hui a été très productif.

examples.text: Os figos desta figueira são muito doces.

translations.de: Die Feigen dieses Feigenbaums sind sehr süß.
translations.en: The figs from this fig tree are very sweet.
translations.fr: Les figues de ce figuier sont très sucrées.

examples.text: Nossa equipe de revisores é muito eficiente.

translations.de: Unser Team von Korrektoren ist sehr effizient.
translations.en: Our team of proofreaders is very efficient.
translations.fr: Notre équipe de relecteurs est très efficace.

examples.text: Estou aprendendo Toki Pona há muito tempo.

translations.fr: J'apprends le toki pona depuis longtemps.

more.definition: very; a lot; very much (to a great extent or degree)

examples.text: Não saímos ontem porque estava muito frio.

translations.de: Wir sind gestern nicht ausgegangen, weil es zu kalt war.
translations.en: We didn't go out yesterday because it was too cold.
translations.fr: Nous ne sommes pas sortis hier car il faisait trop froid.

examples.text: Ele escreveu muitos livros sobre a China.

translations.de: Er hat viele Bücher über China geschrieben.
translations.en: He wrote a lot of books about China.
translations.fr: Il a écrit beaucoup de livres sur la Chine.

translations.de: Ich habe aus diesem Buch viele wichtige Lektionen gelernt.
translations.en: I learned many important lessons from this book.
translations.fr: J'ai appris beaucoup de leçons importantes dans ce livre.

examples.text: Quem muito viajou muita mentira conta.

translations.fr: Ceux qui voyagent beaucoup racontent beaucoup de mensonges.

translations.fr: Ce parc abrite de nombreux oiseaux colorés.

more.definition: much; many; a lot; lots; too much; too many

translations.fr: Peut-on parler d'amour ici ?

translations.fr: Le cerisier est en fleurs. Tout semble plus léger.

translations.fr: Plus je lis des phrases, plus je trouve des erreurs.

translations.de: Die alten Sprachen sind die schwierigsten.
translations.en: The ancient languages are the most difficult.

translations.fr: Je vous aime plus que moi.

translations.fr: Cet arbre a plus d'un siècle.

translations.de: Wasserstoff ist das leichteste Element.
translations.en: Hydrogen is the lightest element.
translations.fr: L'hydrogène est l'élément le plus léger.

translations.de: Qualität ist wichtiger als Quantität.
translations.en: Quality is more important than quantity.
translations.fr: La qualité est plus importante que la quantité.

translations.fr: Tom parle plus lentement que Bill.

translations.fr: La santé vaut plus que l’argent.

translations.en: He's the tallest in the class.
translations.fr: Il est le plus grand de la classe.

translations.fr: Une image vaut mille mots.

examples.text: A África é o continente mais pobre.
