translations.de: Je mehr ich mich anstrenge, desto mehr Fehler mache ich.
translations.en: The more I try, the more mistakes I make.
translations.fr: Plus j'essaye, plus je fais d'erreurs.

examples.text: Estou aposentado há mais de trinta anos.

translations.de: Ich bin seit mehr als dreißig Jahren im Ruhestand.
translations.en: I've been retired for more than thirty years.
translations.fr: Je suis en retraite depuis plus de trente ans.

examples.text: Bilal é mais alto do que Karam.

translations.de: Bilal ist größer als Karam.
translations.en: Bilal is taller than Karam.
translations.fr: Bilal est plus grand que Karam.

examples.text: Fiquei em Boston mais de três meses.

translations.de: Ich blieb über drei Monate in Boston.
translations.en: I stayed in Boston over three months.
translations.fr: Je suis resté à Boston plus de trois mois.

more.etymology: Do latim magis⁽ˡᵃ⁾ “mais”.

more.definition: achar (a spicy and salty pickle of Indian cuisine)
more.etymology: From Hindi आचार (ācār), Malay achar, Urdu آچار (ācār), from Classical Persian آچَار (āčār).

examples.text: Eu acho que nunca vou me casar.

translations.de: Ich vermute, dass ich nie heiraten werde.
translations.en: I guess I'm never going to get married.
translations.fr: Je suppose que je ne me marierai jamais.

examples.text: Você pode achar facilmente o banco.

translations.de: Die Bank kannst du leicht finden.
translations.en: You can easily find the bank.
translations.fr: Tu peux facilement trouver la banque.

examples.text: É bom ter ideais... não achas?

translations.de: Es ist gut, Ideale zu haben, findest du nicht?
translations.en: It is good to have ideals... don't you think?
translations.fr: C'est bien d'avoir des idéaux... tu ne penses pas ?

examples.text: As poltronas eram confortáveis, mas achei as cadeiras incômodas.

translations.de: Die Sessel waren bequem, aber die Stühle fand ich unbequem.
translations.en: The armchairs were comfortable, but I found the chairs uncomfortable.
translations.fr: Les fauteuils étaient confortables, mais j'ai trouvé les chaises inconfortables.

more.definition: to find; to encounter (to come across something that was unknown or had been lost); to find; to consider (to have the opinion that a given thing has the given quality); to find (to come across something in the given state)
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₁-der. Proto-Italic *flāōder. Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese achar, from Latin afflāre. Compare Galician achar and Spanish hallar.

examples.text: Tu não precisas responder a essa pergunta.

translations.de: Du brauchst diese Frage nicht zu beantworten.
translations.en: You don't need to answer that question.
translations.fr: Tu n'as pas besoin de répondre à cette question.

examples.text: Prometo não mais cometer esse erro.

translations.de: Ich verspreche, diesen Fehler nicht noch einmal zu machen.
translations.en: I promise not to make that mistake again.
translations.fr: Je promets de ne plus refaire cette erreur.

examples.text: Nós desapareceremos antes que essas velhas oliveiras desapareçam.

translations.de: Wir werden verschwinden, bevor diese alten Olivenbäume verschwinden.
translations.en: We will disappear before these old olive trees disappear.
translations.fr: Nous disparaîtrons avant que ces vieux oliviers ne disparaissent.

examples.text: Esses carros novos estão a venda.

translations.de: Diese neuen Fahrzeuge stehen zum Verkauf.
translations.en: These new cars are on sale.
translations.fr: Ces nouveaux véhicules sont en vente.

more.definition: that (near you); this (near me)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese esse, from Latin ipse (“himself”).

examples.text: Acho que esse não é o maior problema.

translations.de: Ich denke, das ist nicht das größte Problem.
translations.en: I think that's not the biggest problem.
translations.fr: Je pense que ce n'est pas le plus gros problème.

examples.text: E esse homem era Albert Einstein.

translations.de: Und dieser Mann war Albert Einstein.
translations.en: And that man was Albert Einstein.
translations.fr: Et cet homme était Albert Einstein.

examples.text: Esses políticos confundem a vida pública com a privada.

translations.de: Diese Politiker verwechseln das öffentliche Leben mit dem Privatleben.
translations.en: These politicians confuse public life with private life.
translations.fr: Ces politiciens confondent vie publique et vie privée.

examples.text: Eles estão assistindo a esse filme pela milésima vez.

translations.de: Sie schauen sich diesen Film zum tausendsten Mal an.
translations.en: They are watching this movie for the thousandth time.
translations.fr: Ils regardent ce film pour la millième fois.

more.definition: The name of the Latin script letter S/s.; something shaped like the letter S
idioms: com todos os esses e erres
more.etymology: Pronome: Do latim ipse⁽ˡᵃ⁾.

senses.gloss: nome da décima nona letra do alfabeto latino, representada pelos símbolos "s", "S"

examples.text: Até onde sei, essa função não existe.

translations.de: Soweit ich weiß, gibt es eine solche Funktion nicht.
translations.en: As far as I know, such a function doesn't exist.
translations.fr: Autant que je sache, une telle fonction n'existe pas.

examples.text: Eu não posso mais aguentar esse barulho.

translations.de: Ich kann diesen Lärm nicht mehr ertragen.
translations.en: I can't put up with that noise any longer.
translations.fr: Je ne peux plus supporter ce bruit.

examples.text: Em quanto tempo você fez todas essas coisas?

translations.de: Wie lange haben Sie für all diese Aufgaben gebraucht?
translations.en: How long did it take you to do all these things?
translations.fr: Combien de temps vous a-t-il fallu pour faire tout cela ?

examples.text: Todos esses homens são analfabetos. Não sabem ler nem escrever.

translations.de: All diese Männer sind Analphabeten. Sie können weder lesen noch schreiben.
translations.en: All these men are illiterate. They can neither read nor write.
translations.fr: Tous ces hommes sont analphabètes. Ils ne savent ni lire ni écrire.

more.definition: that, that one (near you); that (that one); this (this one) (indicates something already mentioned or understood from context)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese esse, from Latin ipse (“himself”).

senses.gloss: pronome demonstrativo que designa indivíduo ou objeto afastado de quem fala e próxima da pessoa com quem se fala:

examples.text: Saiam todos daqui. Vão brincar lá fora.

translations.de: Verschwindet alle von hier. Geht draußen spielen.
translations.en: Everyone get out of here. Go play outside.
translations.fr: Sortez tous d'ici. Allez jouer dehors.

examples.text: Ele respondeu todas perguntas em dez minutos.

translations.de: Er beantwortete alle Fragen in zehn Minuten.
translations.en: He answered all the questions in ten minutes.
translations.fr: Il répondit à toutes les questions en dix minutes.

examples.text: Meu pai lê o jornal toda manhã.

translations.de: Mein Vater liest jeden Morgen die Zeitung.
translations.en: My father reads the newspaper every morning.
translations.fr: Mon père lit le journal tous les matins.

examples.text: Eu a amei com todo o meu coração.

translations.de: Ich liebte sie von ganzem Herzen.
translations.en: I loved her with all my heart.
translations.fr: Je l'aimais de tout mon cœur.

more.definition: whole, entire
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese todo, from Latin tōtus, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *tewtéh₂ (“people; tribe”). Compare Galician and Spanish todo, Catalan tot, French tout, Italian tutto, and Romanian tot.

examples.text: Vejo aquele cachorro quase todos os dias.

translations.de: Ich sehe diesen Hund fast jeden Tag.
translations.en: I see that dog almost every day.
translations.fr: Je vois le chien presque tous les jours.

examples.text: Estou farto de todas as mentiras deles.

translations.de: Ich habe all ihre Lügen satt.
translations.en: I'm fed up with all their lies.
translations.fr: Je suis fatigué de tous leurs mensonges.

examples.text: Ele perdeu todo o interesse pelas línguas artificiais.

translations.de: Er verlor jegliches Interesse an künstlichen Sprachen.
translations.en: He lost all interest in artificial languages.
translations.fr: Il a perdu tout intérêt pour les langues artificielles.

examples.text: Nem toda frase pode ser escrita em verso.

translations.de: Nicht jeder Satz kann in Versform geschrieben werden.
translations.en: Not every sentence can be written in verse.
translations.fr: Toutes les phrases ne peuvent pas être écrites en vers.

more.definition: all (wholly; completely)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese todo, from Latin tōtus, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *tewtéh₂ (“people; tribe”). Compare Galician and Spanish todo, Catalan tot, French tout, Italian tutto, and Romanian tot.

examples.text: Fazemos uma caminhada todos os dias.

translations.de: Wir machen jeden Tag einen Spaziergang.
translations.en: We go for a walk every day.
translations.fr: Nous allons nous promener tous les jours.

examples.text: O tempo consome todas as coisas.

translations.de: Die Zeit verzehrt alles.
translations.en: Time consumes all things.
translations.fr: Le temps consume toute chose.

examples.text: O trem para em toda estação.

translations.de: Der Zug hält an jeder Station.
translations.en: The train stops at every station.
translations.fr: Le train s'arrête à chaque station.

examples.text: Seu nome é conhecido em todo o país.

translations.de: Sein Name ist im ganzen Land bekannt.
translations.en: His name is known all over the country.
translations.fr: Son nom est connu dans tout le pays.

more.definition: every; all (all of a group); whole, entire
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese todo, from Latin tōtus, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *tewtéh₂ (“people; tribe”). Compare Galician and Spanish todo, Catalan tot, French tout, Italian tutto, and Romanian tot.

examples.text: Tenho um amigo em que todos confiam.

translations.de: Ich habe einen Freund, dem jeder vertraut.
translations.en: I have a friend everybody trusts.
translations.fr: J'ai un ami en qui tout le monde à confiance.

examples.text: Que é que todo o mundo está olhando?

translations.de: Worauf schauen alle?
translations.en: What's everybody looking at?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que tout le monde regarde ?

examples.text: Um por todos e todos por um.

translations.de: Einer für alle, alle für einen.
translations.en: One for all and all for one.
translations.fr: Un pour tous, tous pour un.

examples.text: Eu estudo turco todos os dias.

translations.de: Ich lerne jeden Tag Türkisch.
translations.en: I study Turkish every day.
translations.fr: J'étudie le turc tous les jours.

more.definition: whole (something complete)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese todo, from Latin tōtus, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *tewtéh₂ (“people; tribe”). Compare Galician and Spanish todo, Catalan tot, French tout, Italian tutto, and Romanian tot.

examples.text: É louco quem pretende agradar a todo o mundo.

translations.de: Wer versucht, es allen recht zu machen, ist verrückt.
translations.en: Anyone who tries to please everyone is crazy.
translations.fr: Quiconque essaie de plaire à tout le monde est fou.

examples.text: Tom comeu todo o chocolate.

translations.de: Tom hat die ganze Schokolade gegessen.
translations.en: Tom ate all of the chocolate.
translations.fr: Tom a mangé tout le chocolat.

examples.text: Ken me liga todo dia.

translations.de: Ken ruft mich jeden Tag an.
translations.en: Ken calls me every day.
translations.fr: Ken me téléphone tous les jours.

examples.text: A pobreza é a raiz de todo o mal.

translations.de: Armut ist die Wurzel allen Übels.
translations.en: Poverty is the root of all evil.
translations.fr: La pauvreté est à la racine de tout mal.

more.etymology: Do latim totus⁽ˡᵃ⁾.

examples.text: Essa é uma boa ideia.

translations.de: Das ist eine gute Idee.
translations.en: This is a good idea.
translations.fr: C'est une bonne idée.

examples.text: A comida aqui é muito boa.

translations.de: Das Essen hier ist sehr gut.
translations.en: The food here is very good.
translations.fr: La nourriture ici est très bonne.

examples.text: Eu e o Tom somos bons amigos.

translations.de: Tom und ich sind gute Freunde.
translations.en: Tom and I are good friends.
translations.fr: Tom et moi sommes de bons amis.

examples.text: Hoje à noite assistiremos a um bom filme.

translations.de: Heute Abend schauen wir uns einen guten Film an.
translations.en: Tonight we'll watch a good movie.
translations.fr: Ce soir, nous regarderons un bon film.

examples.text: Com uma caneta boa escrevemos melhor.

translations.de: Mit einem guten Stift schreiben wir besser.
translations.en: With a good pen, we write better.
translations.fr: Avec un bon stylo, on écrit mieux.

examples.text: Os maus costumes geram boas leis.

translations.de: Schlechte Angewohnheiten führen zu guten Gesetzen.
translations.en: Bad habits breed good laws.
translations.fr: Les mauvaises habitudes engendrent les bonnes lois.

more.definition: desirable, positive, advantageous; pleasant, enjoyable, (of food) tasty; kind, generous, acting morally
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese bõo, inherited from Latin bonus (“good”), from Old Latin duonos, earlier duenos, from Proto-Italic *dwenos. Doublet of bónus /bônus, a later borrowing. Compare Fala and Galician bo, Spanish bueno.

senses.gloss: que corresponde plenamente ao que é exigido, desejado ou esperado quanto à sua natureza, adequação, função, eficácia, funcionamento etc. (falando de ser ou coisa)

examples.text: Ele não é um bom professor?

translations.de: Ist er nicht ein guter Lehrer?
translations.en: Isn't he a good teacher?
translations.fr: N'est-il pas un bon professeur ?

examples.text: E viu Deus que era bom.

translations.de: Und Gott sah, dass es gut war.
translations.en: And God saw that it was good.
translations.fr: Et Dieu vit que cela était bon.

examples.text: Se a frase tem bom ritmo, está certa.

translations.de: Wenn der Satz einen guten Rhythmus hat, ist er richtig.
translations.en: If the sentence has a good rhythm, it's alright.
translations.fr: Si la phrase a un bon rythme, c'est juste.

examples.text: Você é bom, mas seu amigo é muito mau.

translations.de: Du bist gut, aber dein Freund ist sehr böse.
translations.en: You are good, but your friend is very bad.
translations.fr: Tu es bon, mais ton ami est très mauvais.

more.definition: well, very well
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese bõo, inherited from Latin bonus (“good”), from Old Latin duonos, earlier duenos, from Proto-Italic *dwenos. Doublet of bónus /bônus, a later borrowing. Compare Fala and Galician bo, Spanish bueno.

examples.text: Aprecio teu bom humor. Achas tudo engraçado.

translations.de: Ich schätze deinen guten Humor. Du findest alles lustig.
translations.en: I appreciate your good humor. You find everything funny.
translations.fr: J'apprécie ta bonne humeur. Tu trouves tout drôle.

examples.text: O bom aluno agora ensina ao professor.

translations.de: Der gute Schüler unterrichtet nun den Lehrer.
translations.en: The good student now teaches the teacher.
translations.fr: Le bon élève enseigne désormais au professeur.

examples.text: Isso é bom demais para ser verdade.

translations.de: Das ist zu schön, um wahr zu sein.
translations.en: This is too good to be true.
translations.fr: C'est trop beau pour être vrai.

examples.text: Você pode me recomendar um bom dicionário?

translations.de: Kannst du mir ein gutes Wörterbuch empfehlen?
translations.en: Can you recommend a good dictionary to me?
translations.fr: Peux-tu me recommander un bon dictionnaire?

more.etymology: Do galego-português medieval bon, de bõo, através do latim bonum, acusativo de bonus e este da sua forma anterior duonus de duenos.

examples.text: Eu quero que tudo esteja perfeito.

translations.de: Ich möchte, dass alles perfekt ist.
translations.en: I want everything to be just right.
translations.fr: Je veux que tout soit parfait.

examples.text: Você fez tudo isso hoje?

translations.de: Hast du das alles heute erledigt?
translations.en: Did you do all that today?
translations.fr: Avez-vous fait tout cela aujourd'hui ?

examples.text: Quando você vai ter tempo de fazer tudo isso?

translations.de: Wann haben Sie Zeit für all das?
translations.en: When will you have time to do all this?
translations.fr: Quand aurez-vous le temps de faire tout cela ?

examples.text: Tu és tudo para mim.

translations.de: Du bist alles für mich.
translations.en: You're very dear to me.
translations.fr: Tu es tout pour moi.

more.definition: everything (all the things); everything that is essential; everyone; all (all people in general or in a specific group)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese todo, from Latin tōtus (“all; everything”).

examples.text: Este dia vai ficar para a história.

translations.de: Dieser Tag wird in die Geschichte eingehen.
translations.en: This day will go down in history.
translations.fr: Ce jour entrera dans l'histoire.

examples.text: Os correios também ficam nesta rua.

translations.de: Das Postamt befindet sich ebenfalls in dieser Straße.
translations.en: The post office is also on this street.
translations.fr: Le bureau de poste se trouve également dans cette rue.

examples.text: Esse restaurante não fica nesta rua.

translations.de: Dieses Restaurant befindet sich nicht in dieser Straße.
translations.en: This restaurant is not located on this street.
translations.fr: Ce restaurant ne se trouve pas dans cette rue.

examples.text: Parte da ilha ficou devastada pelas ondas gigantes.

translations.de: Ein Teil der Insel wurde durch die riesigen Wellen zerstört.
translations.en: A portion of the island was destroyed by the massive waves.
translations.fr: Une partie de l'île a été détruite par les vagues géantes.

more.definition: to become; to get; to end up; to be, to be located; to stay (at); to remain (in)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese ficar (also fincar), from Vulgar Latin *fīg(i)cāre, frequentative based on Latin fīgere (“drive in, fix in place”). Doublet of fincar.

examples.text: Eu só fiz o meu dever.

translations.de: Ich tat nur meine Pflicht.
translations.en: I only did my duty.
translations.fr: Je ne fis que mon devoir.

examples.text: Será que estamos sós nessa infinitude que é o universo?

translations.de: Sind wir allein in der Unendlichkeit des Universums?
translations.en: Are we alone in this infinity that is the universe?
translations.fr: Sommes-nous seuls dans cet infini qu’est l’univers ?

examples.text: Nós todos somos filhos. O Pai é um só.

translations.de: Wir sind alle Kinder. Es gibt nur einen Vater.
translations.en: We are all children. There is only one Father.
translations.fr: Nous sommes tous des enfants. Il n'y a qu'un seul Père.

examples.text: Em Atenas comprei um papagaio que só fala Grego.

translations.de: In Athen habe ich einen Papagei gekauft, der nur Griechisch spricht.
translations.en: In Athens, I bought a parrot that only speaks Greek.
translations.fr: À Athènes, j'ai acheté un perroquet qui ne parle que le grec.

more.definition: only; just (alone in a category); only; just (no more than); only; merely; just (introduces a number or object with the implication that it is small or insufficient)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese soo, from Latin sōlus (“alone”). Doublet of solo.

senses.gloss: solitário, sem companhia, sem círculo social

examples.text: Não só de pão vive o homem.

translations.de: Der Mensch lebt nicht vom Brot allein.
translations.en: Man does not live by bread alone.
translations.fr: Ce n'est pas de pain seul que vivra l'homme.

examples.text: Eu falo turco só um pouquinho.

translations.de: Ich spreche Türkisch, aber nur ein bisschen.
translations.en: I speak just a little bit of Turkish.
translations.fr: Je parle turc, mais seulement un peu.

examples.text: Toki Pona só tem palavras para números pequenos.

translations.de: Toki Pona hat nur Wörter für kleine Zahlen.
translations.en: Toki Pona only has words for small numbers.
translations.fr: Toki Pona n'a de mots que pour les petits nombres.

examples.text: O Tom é só um iniciante.

translations.de: Tom ist erst Anfänger.
translations.en: Tom is only a beginner.
translations.fr: Tom est seulement débutant.

more.definition: only; just (indicates that no other action is/was/will be performed); only; merely; just; simply (indicates that the action is not significant); alone (unaccompanied or without help)
idioms: antes só do que mal acompanhado
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese soo, from Latin sōlus (“alone”). Doublet of solo.

examples.text: Ele só tem uma perna.

translations.de: Er hat nur ein Bein.
translations.en: He has only one leg.
translations.fr: Il n'a qu'une seule jambe.

examples.text: Isso é só um brinquedo.

translations.de: Das ist doch nur ein Spielzeug.
translations.en: That's only a toy.
translations.fr: C'est seulement un jouet.

examples.text: Eu só quero pegar um pouco de ar fresco.

translations.de: Ich will einfach nur etwas frische Luft schnappen.
translations.en: I just want to get a little fresh air.
translations.fr: Je veux simplement prendre un peu d'air frais.

examples.text: Não gosto de ficar só.

translations.de: Ich bin nicht gern allein.
translations.en: I dislike being alone.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas être seul.

examples.text: Eu gosto desse traço da personalidade dele.

translations.de: Ich mag diese Persönlichkeitseigenschaft von ihm.
translations.en: I like this trait of his personality.
translations.fr: J'aime ce trait de caractère qu'il a.

examples.text: Tenho vontade de lhe dar mil beijos.

translations.de: Ich möchte ihm tausend Küsse geben.
translations.en: I want to give you a thousand kisses.
translations.fr: J'ai envie de lui faire 1000 bisous.

examples.text: Eu não responderei às perguntas maliciosas desses jornalistas.

translations.de: Ich werde die böswilligen Fragen dieser Journalisten nicht beantworten.
translations.en: I will not answer these journalists' malicious questions.
translations.fr: Je ne répondrai pas aux questions malveillantes de ces journalistes.

examples.text: Ela me deu três filhos e uma filha.

translations.de: Sie schenkte mir drei Söhne und eine Tochter.
translations.en: She gave me three sons and a daughter.
translations.fr: Elle m'a donné trois fils et une fille.

more.definition: to transfer one’s possession of something to someone without anything in return; to hand over (to pass something into someone’s hand); to make a present or gift of
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese dar (“to give”), from Latin dare, from Proto-Italic *didō, from Proto-Indo-European *dédeh₃ti, from the root *deh₃- (“give”).

senses.gloss: transferir a posse de algo, gratuitamente, para outrem

examples.text: Era então inverno.

translations.de: Damals war es Winter.
translations.en: It was winter then.
translations.fr: C'était alors l'hiver.

examples.text: Se os robôs fizerem tudo, o que então os humanos vão fazer?

translations.de: Wenn Roboter alles tun, was werden die Menschen dann tun?
translations.en: If robots do everything, what then will humans do?
translations.fr: Si les robots font tout, que feront les humains ?

examples.text: Se algo não é proibido, então é permitido?

translations.de: Wenn etwas nicht verboten ist, ist es dann erlaubt?
translations.en: If something is not forbidden, then is it allowed?
translations.fr: Si une chose n'est pas interdite, alors est-elle permise ?

examples.text: Se não há solução, então não há problema.

translations.de: Wenn es keine Lösung gibt, dann gibt es kein Problem.
translations.en: If there's no solution, then there's no problem.
translations.fr: S'il n'y a pas de solution, alors il n'y a pas de problème.

more.definition: then (at that time); then (soon afterwards; after that)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese enton, from Vulgar Latin *in tunc, from Latin in + tunc (“then”). Displaced collateral form entonce. Compare Spanish entonces.

examples.text: E então, mudou de ideia?

translations.de: Also, haben Sie Ihre Meinung geändert?
translations.en: So, have you changed your mind?
translations.fr: Alors, vous avez changé d'avis ?

examples.text: Então, percebi que havia algo mais no horizonte.

translations.de: Dann wurde mir klar, dass da noch etwas anderes am Horizont lauerte.
translations.en: Now I felt there was more in the offing.
translations.fr: Je sentais maintenant qu'il y avait autre chose en perspective.

examples.text: Era então inverno.

translations.de: Damals war es Winter.
translations.en: It was winter then.
translations.fr: C'était alors l'hiver.

examples.text: Se os robôs fizerem tudo, o que então os humanos vão fazer?

translations.de: Wenn Roboter alles tun, was werden die Menschen dann tun?
translations.en: If robots do everything, what then will humans do?
translations.fr: Si les robots font tout, que feront les humains ?

more.definition: thus; therefore (as a result)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese enton, from Vulgar Latin *in tunc, from Latin in + tunc (“then”). Displaced collateral form entonce. Compare Spanish entonces.

examples.text: Se algo não é proibido, então é permitido?

translations.de: Wenn etwas nicht verboten ist, ist es dann erlaubt?
translations.en: If something is not forbidden, then is it allowed?
translations.fr: Si une chose n'est pas interdite, alors est-elle permise ?

examples.text: Se não há solução, então não há problema.

translations.de: Wenn es keine Lösung gibt, dann gibt es kein Problem.
translations.en: If there's no solution, then there's no problem.
translations.fr: S'il n'y a pas de solution, alors il n'y a pas de problème.

examples.text: E então, mudou de ideia?

translations.de: Also, haben Sie Ihre Meinung geändert?
translations.en: So, have you changed your mind?
translations.fr: Alors, vous avez changé d'avis ?

examples.text: Então, percebi que havia algo mais no horizonte.

translations.de: Dann wurde mir klar, dass da noch etwas anderes am Horizont lauerte.
translations.en: Now I felt there was more in the offing.
translations.fr: Je sentais maintenant qu'il y avait autre chose en perspective.

more.definition: so (used after a pause for thought to introduce a new topic, question or story); Used to introduce an answer which is more complex than expected.; exactly (signifies agreement or recognition).
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese enton, from Vulgar Latin *in tunc, from Latin in + tunc (“then”). Displaced collateral form entonce. Compare Spanish entonces.

examples.text: Eu estou aprendendo francês agora.

translations.de: Ich lerne jetzt Französisch.
translations.en: I'm learning French now.
translations.fr: J'apprends le français maintenant.

examples.text: Sinto-me muito melhor agora.

translations.de: Mir geht es jetzt schon viel besser.
translations.en: I'm feeling much better now.
translations.fr: Je vais beaucoup mieux maintenant.

examples.text: Não preciso me levantar agora. Vou dormir mais um pouco.

translations.de: Ich muss jetzt nicht aufstehen. Ich schlafe noch ein bisschen.
translations.en: I don't need to get up right now. I'm going to sleep a little longer.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas besoin de me lever maintenant. Je vais dormir encore un peu.

examples.text: Ele era muito trabalhador, mas agora está um pouco preguiçoso.

translations.de: Früher war er sehr fleißig, aber jetzt ist er etwas faul.
translations.en: He used to be very hardworking, but now he's a bit lazy.
translations.fr: Avant, il était très travailleur, mais maintenant, il est un peu paresseux.

more.definition: now; right now (at the present time); now; any more (differently from the past); just now (very recently)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese agora, from Latin hāc hōrā. Compare Galician agora and Spanish ahora. To a lesser extent, compare also Italian ora and Old French ore.

examples.text: Eu não posso te explicar agora.

translations.de: Ich kann dir das jetzt nicht erklären.
translations.en: I cannot explain it to you now.
translations.fr: Je ne peux te l'expliquer maintenant.

examples.text: O navio está agora no porto.

translations.de: Das Schiff ist jetzt im Hafen.
translations.en: The ship is now in the harbor.
translations.fr: Le bateau est maintenant au port.

examples.text: Você não pode me deixar agora!

translations.de: Du kannst mich jetzt nicht sitzenlassen.
translations.en: You can't leave me now.
translations.fr: Tu ne peux pas me laisser maintenant.

examples.text: Minha mãe está no hospital agora.

translations.de: Meine Mutter ist jetzt im Krankenhaus.
translations.en: My mother is in the hospital now.
translations.fr: Ma mère est à l'hôpital, en ce moment.

more.definition: on the other hand; whereas; while (introduces an example that is the opposite of the previous example); sometimes … sometimes
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese agora, from Latin hāc hōrā. Compare Galician agora and Spanish ahora. To a lesser extent, compare also Italian ora and Old French ore.

examples.text: Acredito que agora seja o momento certo.

translations.de: Ich denke, dass jetzt der richtige Zeitpunkt ist.
translations.en: I think that the right time is right now.
translations.fr: Je pense que le bon moment, c'est maintenant.

examples.text: Eu chorei por você. Chore agora por mim.

translations.de: Ich habe um dich geweint. Jetzt weine du um mich.
translations.en: I cried for you. Now cry for me.
translations.fr: J'ai pleuré pour toi. Pleure maintenant pour moi.

examples.text: A frase está mais clara agora?

translations.de: Ist der Satz jetzt verständlicher?
translations.en: Is the sentence clearer now?
translations.fr: La phrase est-elle plus claire maintenant ?

examples.text: Quem ri agora, há de chorar mais tarde.

translations.de: Wer jetzt lacht, wird später weinen.
translations.en: Whoever laughs now will cry later.
translations.fr: Celui qui rit maintenant pleurera plus tard.

more.etymology: Do latim hac (hora).

examples.text: Gostaria de ir para casa agora.

translations.de: Ich würde jetzt gerne nach Hause gehen.
translations.en: I would like to go home now.
translations.fr: Je voudrais aller à la maison maintenant.

examples.text: Meu pai está no hospital agora.

translations.de: Mein Vater ist jetzt im Krankenhaus.
translations.en: My father is in the hospital now.
translations.fr: Mon père est maintenant à l'hôpital.

examples.text: Ele era muito pobre, mas agora é muito rico.

translations.de: Er war sehr arm, aber jetzt ist er sehr reich.
translations.en: He used to be very poor, but now he is very rich.
translations.fr: Il était très pauvre, mais il est désormais très riche.

examples.text: Tom está em Boston agora.

translations.de: Tom ist jetzt in Boston.
translations.en: Tom is in Boston now.
translations.fr: Tom est à Boston maintenant.

more.definition: now (the present time)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese agora, from Latin hāc hōrā. Compare Galician agora and Spanish ahora. To a lesser extent, compare also Italian ora and Old French ore.

examples.text: Meu filhinho está aprendendo a falar.

translations.de: Mein kleiner Junge lernt sprechen.
translations.en: My little son is learning to talk.
translations.fr: Mon petit garçon apprend à parler.

more.definition: a cant, dialect or regional language
more.etymology: Nominalization of Etymology 1.

examples.text: Não fale dessa mulher perto de mim.

translations.de: Sprechen Sie in meiner Gegenwart nicht über diese Frau!
translations.en: Don't talk about that woman near me.
translations.fr: Ne parle pas de cette femme près de moi.

examples.text: Eu ainda não sei falar turco.

translations.de: Ich kann immer noch kein Türkisch sprechen.
translations.en: I still don't know how to speak Turkish.
translations.fr: Je ne sais toujours pas parler turc.

examples.text: O nosso professor fala catorze línguas.

translations.de: Unser Lehrer spricht vierzehn Sprachen.
translations.en: Our teacher speaks fourteen languages.
translations.fr: Notre professeur parle quatorze langues.

examples.text: Nem todos os irmãos falam a mesma língua.

translations.de: Nicht alle Brüder sprechen die gleiche Sprache.
translations.en: Not all brothers speak the same language.
translations.fr: Tous les frères ne parlent pas la même langue.

more.definition: to speak; to talk (to say words out loud); to communicate by any means; to say something
idioms: falar mais que o homem da cobra
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese falar, from Latin fābulārī (“chat, converse”). Doublet of fabular, which was borrowed from Latin. Compare Galician falar, Spanish hablar.

examples.text: Este trabalho é qualquer coisa menos fácil.

translations.de: Diese Arbeit ist alles andere als leicht.
translations.en: This work is anything but easy.
translations.fr: Ce travail est tout sauf facile.

examples.text: Os gregos fizeram muitas coisas importantes.

translations.de: Die Griechen taten viele wichtige Dinge.
translations.en: The Greeks did many important things.
translations.fr: Les Grecs ont fait beaucoup de choses importantes.

examples.text: Ele havia pensado em muitas coisas.

translations.de: Er hatte an viele Dinge gedacht.
translations.en: He had thought of a lot of things.
translations.fr: Il avait pensé à beaucoup de choses.

examples.text: Ninguém é velho demais para aprender coisas novas.

translations.de: Es ist nie zu spät zum Lernen.
translations.en: Nobody is too old to learn new things.
translations.fr: Personne n'est trop vieux pour apprendre.

more.definition: thing (a physical object, entity, or situation); thingamajig; gizmo, thingy (something whose name is unknown)
more.etymology: Alteration of cousa, from Old Galician-Portuguese cousa, from Latin causa (“cause, reason”), meaning "thing" in Late and Vulgar Latin. Doublet of causa, a learned borrowing. Compare Galician cousa, Spanish, Italian, and Catalan cosa, and French chose.

senses.gloss: qualquer objeto inanimado; em sentido filosófico, coisa é tudo aquilo subsistente por si mesmo; a filosofia kantiana afirma ser uma coisa aquilo que existe independentemente do espírito; no sentido usual, como para o Direito, coisa é tudo aquilo que, percebido pelos sentidos, pode apresentar utilidade para o homem, caso em que se chama bem material

examples.text: Em meu viver se fez noite quando você foi embora.

translations.de: In meinem Leben wurde es Nacht, als du gegangen bist.
translations.en: In my life it became night when you left.
translations.fr: Dans ma vie, c'est devenu la nuit quand tu es partie.

examples.text: As palavras turcas geralmente ganham sentido quando se conhecem suas partes.

translations.de: Türkische Wörter sind im Allgemeinen verständlich, wenn man ihre Bestandteile kennt.
translations.en: Turkish words generally make sense when their parts are known.
translations.fr: Les mots turcs ont généralement un sens lorsqu'on connaît leurs composants.

examples.text: Meu irmão dançava com a esposa quando sofreu um infarto fulminante.

translations.de: Mein Bruder tanzte gerade mit seiner Frau, als er einen tödlichen Herzinfarkt erlitt.
translations.en: My brother was dancing with his wife when he suffered a fatal heart attack.
translations.fr: Mon frère dansait avec sa femme lorsqu'il a été victime d'une crise cardiaque fatale.

examples.text: Quando o ar está mais quente, chove mais.

translations.de: Wenn die Luft wärmer ist, regnet es mehr.
translations.en: When the air is warmer, it rains more.
translations.fr: Quand l'air est plus chaud, il pleut davantage.

more.definition: when (used in questions about time); when (during which)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese quando, from Latin quandō.

examples.text: Eu estava lá quando ela entrou.

translations.de: Ich war dort, als sie hereinkam.
translations.en: I was there when she walked in.
translations.fr: J'étais là quand elle est entrée.

examples.text: Eu tinha oitenta anos quando meu neto nasceu.

translations.de: Ich war achtzig Jahre alt, als mein Enkel geboren wurde.
translations.en: I was eighty years old when my grandson was born.
translations.fr: J'avais quatre-vingts ans quand mon petit-fils est né.

examples.text: O mar, quando está calmo, espelha o céu.

translations.de: Wenn es ruhig ist, spiegelt das Meer den Himmel.
translations.en: The sea, when it is calm, mirrors the sky.
translations.fr: La mer, quand elle est calme, reflète le ciel.

examples.text: Desde quando ele mora em Ankara?

translations.de: Seit wann lebt er schon in Ankara?
translations.en: Since when has he been living in Ankara?
translations.fr: Depuis quand vit-il à Ankara ?

more.definition: when (at such time); when (whilst on the contrary)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese quando, from Latin quandō.

examples.text: Olhe para mim quando eu falar com você!

translations.de: Sieh mich an, wenn ich mit dir spreche!
translations.en: Look at me when I talk to you!
translations.fr: Regarde-moi quand je te parle !

examples.text: Eu não gosto de sair quando está chovendo.

translations.de: Ich gehe nicht gerne nach draußen, wenn es regnet.
translations.en: I don't like to go outside when it's raining.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas sortir quand il pleut.

examples.text: A minha alma nasceu quando se fez a luz.

translations.de: Meine Seele wurde geboren, als Licht gemacht wurde.
translations.en: My soul was born when the light was made.
translations.fr: Mon âme est née quand la lumière a été faite.

examples.text: O menino caiu de medo quando viu um fantasma.

translations.de: Der Junge bekam Angst, als er einen Geist sah.
translations.en: The boy fell of fright when he saw a ghost.
translations.fr: Le garçon est tombé de peur quand il a vu un fantôme.

more.definition: when (a point or period in time)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese quando, from Latin quandō.

examples.text: Dedico este livro à minha filha.

translations.de: Ich widme dieses Buch meiner Tochter.
translations.en: I dedicate this book to my daughter.
translations.fr: Je dédie ce livre à ma fille.

examples.text: Estes papagaios são meus. Os teus são aqueles.

translations.de: Diese Papageien sind meine. Deine sind die.
translations.en: These parrots are mine. Yours are those.
translations.fr: Ces perroquets sont à moi. Les tiens sont ceux-là.

examples.text: Foi você quem fez este bolo? Está uma delícia!

translations.de: Hast du diesen Kuchen gebacken? Er schmeckt köstlich!
translations.en: Was it you who made this cake? It's delicious!
translations.fr: C'est vous qui avez fait ce gâteau ? Il est délicieux !

examples.text: De quem é este vestido?

translations.de: Wem gehört dieses Kleid?
translations.en: Whose dress is this?
translations.fr: À qui appartient cette robe ?

more.definition: eastern (of, situated in, or coming from the east)
more.etymology: Borrowed from French est, from Old English ēast, from Proto-Germanic *austrą (“east”), from Proto-Indo-European *aus- (“eastern”).

examples.text: Não tenho tempo para ler este livro.

translations.de: Ich habe keine Zeit, dieses Buch zu lesen.
translations.en: I don't have the time to read this book.
translations.fr: Je n'ai pas le temps de lire ce livre.

examples.text: Que fizemos de errado para merecer esta penalidade?

translations.de: Was haben wir falsch gemacht, dass wir diese Sanktion verdienen?
translations.en: What did we do wrong to deserve this sanction?
translations.fr: Qu’avons-nous fait de mal pour mériter cette pénalité ?

examples.text: Eu não posso comer este tipo de alimento.

translations.de: Ich kann diese Art Nahrung nicht essen.
translations.en: I can't eat this kind of food.
translations.fr: Je ne peux pas manger ce genre de nourriture.

examples.text: Eu não quero comprar este tapete.

translations.de: Ich möchte diesen Teppich nicht kaufen.
translations.en: I don't want to buy this carpet.
translations.fr: Je ne veux pas acheter ce tapis.

more.definition: this (indicates something or someone nearby); that (indicates something or someone just mentioned); this (indicates something or someone about to be mentioned)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese este (displacing collateral form aqueste), from Latin iste.

examples.text: Onde você comprou este livro?

translations.de: Wo haben Sie dieses Buch gekauft?
translations.en: Where did you buy this book?
translations.fr: Où as-tu acheté ce livre ?

examples.text: Quem te vendeu este carro?

translations.de: Wer hat dir diesen Wagen verkauft?
translations.en: Who sold you this car?
translations.fr: Qui t'a vendu cette voiture ?

examples.text: O próximo trem estará menos cheio que este aqui.

translations.de: Der nächste Zug ist weniger voll als dieser hier.
translations.en: The next train will be less crowded than this one.
translations.fr: Le prochain train sera moins plein que celui-ci.

examples.text: Tu podes resolver este problema?

translations.de: Können Sie dieses Problem lösen?
translations.en: Can you solve this problem?
translations.fr: Peux-tu résoudre ce problème ?

more.definition: east (one of the four principal compass points)
more.etymology: Borrowed from French est, from Old English ēast, from Proto-Germanic *austrą (“east”), from Proto-Indo-European *aus- (“eastern”).

examples.text: Você pode cuidar do bebê esta tarde?

translations.de: Kannst du dich heute Nachmittag um das Baby kümmern?
translations.en: Can you look after the baby this afternoon?
translations.fr: Pouvez-vous garder le bébé cet après-midi ?

examples.text: É este um garanhão ou uma égua?

translations.de: Ist das ein Hengst oder eine Stute?
translations.en: Is this a stallion or a mare?
translations.fr: Est-ce un étalon ou une jument ?

examples.text: Você encontrou a diferença entre estas duas fotos?

translations.de: Hast du den Unterschied zwischen diesen zwei Fotos entdeckt?
translations.en: Did you find the difference between these two photos?
translations.fr: Tu as découvert la différence entre ces deux photos ?

examples.text: Você deve copiar esta frase cem vezes.

translations.de: Du musst diesen Satz hundertmal kopieren.
translations.en: You must copy this sentence one hundred times.
translations.fr: Il faut que tu copies cette phrase cent fois.

more.definition: this one (indicates something or someone nearby); this one (indicates something or someone about to be mentioned); this (which is current)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese este (displacing collateral form aqueste), from Latin iste.

senses.gloss: relativo a alguém ou alguma coisa que esteja perto de quem fala:

examples.text: Pode-se dizer de ambas as maneiras, certo?

translations.de: Man kann es in beide Richtungen sagen, oder?
translations.en: You can say it both ways, right?
translations.fr: On peut le dire dans les deux sens, n'est-ce pas ?

examples.text: A primeira resposta está certa, a segunda está errada.

translations.de: Die erste Antwort ist richtig, die zweite ist falsch.
translations.en: The first answer is correct; the second is wrong.
translations.fr: La première réponse est correcte, la seconde est fausse.

examples.text: Você usou uma camisinha para não engravidar, certo?

translations.de: Du hast zur Empfängnisverhütung ein Kondom benutzt, nicht wahr?
translations.en: You used a condom for birth control, right?
translations.fr: Vous utilisez un préservatif pour ne pas tomber enceinte, n'est-ce pas ?

examples.text: Certo. O que eu posso fazer?

translations.de: Natürlich. Was kann ich tun?
translations.en: Certainly. What can I do?
translations.fr: Bien sûr. Que puis-je faire ?

more.definition: right; correct (not containing errors); certain; sure (without doubt); precise; accurate
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese certo, from Latin certus (“certain”), past participle of cernō (“to sift; to discern”), from Proto-Indo-European *krey- (“to move; to separate”).

translations.fr: Vous utilisez un préservatif pour ne pas tomber enceinte, n'est-ce pas ?

examples.text: Certo. O que eu posso fazer?

translations.de: Natürlich. Was kann ich tun?

translations.fr: Bien sûr. Que puis-je faire ?

translations.fr: Même une montre cassée donne l'heure exacte deux fois par jour.

examples.text: Ela se apaixonou por um certo príncipe.

translations.de: Sie hat sich in einen bestimmten Prinzen verliebt.

translations.fr: Elle est tombée amoureuse d'un certain prince.
