more.definition: to wait (for); to await; to wait; to hope for (to really want)
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *-h₂tiinflu. Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese asperar, from Latin spērāre, from Old Latin *spēsō, from spēs (“hope”) + -ō (verbal suffix).

senses.gloss: ter esperança; aguardar com desejo e uma certa confiança de que algo vá se realizar

examples.text: Lá vem o trem.

translations.de: Da kommt der Zug.
translations.en: There comes the train.
translations.fr: Voilà le train.

examples.text: Eu estava lá quando ela entrou.

translations.de: Ich war dort, als sie hereinkam.
translations.en: I was there when she walked in.
translations.fr: J'étais là quand elle est entrée.

examples.text: Parece que chegaremos lá a tempo.

translations.de: Es scheint, dass wir dort rechtzeitig ankommen werden.
translations.en: It looks like we'll get there in time.
translations.fr: Il semble que nous y parviendrons à temps.

examples.text: Quantas vezes você foi lá?

translations.de: Wie oft bist du dahin gegangen?
translations.en: How many times have you gone there?
translations.fr: Combien de fois es-tu allé là ?

more.definition: there (in that place, far from both the speaker and the audience); used with an adverb phrase to indicate that something is far; used to emphasize a relative distant point in the past or in the future
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese ala, from Latin ad (“to”) + illāc (“that way”).

examples.text: Como posso chegar lá?

translations.de: Wie komme ich dorthin?
translations.en: How can I get there?
translations.fr: Comment puis-je y arriver ?

examples.text: O carro não está na garagem. Quem o tirou de lá?

translations.de: Das Auto ist nicht in der Garage. Wer hat es von dort mitgenommen?
translations.en: The car isn't in the garage. Who took it from there?
translations.fr: La voiture n'est pas dans le garage. Qui l'a prise ?

examples.text: Ele foi ao Egito e de lá trouxe de volta a filha.

translations.de: Er reiste nach Ägypten und brachte seine Tochter von dort mit.
translations.en: He went to Egypt and brought his daughter back from there.
translations.fr: Il est allé en Égypte et en a ramené sa fille.

examples.text: Saiam todos daqui. Vão brincar lá fora.

translations.de: Verschwindet alle von hier. Geht draußen spielen.
translations.en: Everyone get out of here. Go play outside.
translations.fr: Sortez tous d'ici. Allez jouer dehors.

more.definition: la (sixth note of a major scale, in solfège)
more.etymology: Borrowed from Italian la, from the first syllable of Latin labiī (“lip’s”).

examples.text: A violência começa onde a paciência acaba.

translations.de: Gewalt fängt dort an, wo Geduld aufhört.
translations.en: Violence begins where patience ends.
translations.fr: La violence commence là où la patience s'arrête.

examples.text: Meu lar é o lugar onde você estiver.

translations.de: Mein Zuhause ist da, wo du bist.
translations.en: My home is wherever you are.
translations.fr: Ma maison est là où tu es.

examples.text: Você sabe onde fica a farmácia mais próxima?

translations.de: Wissen Sie, wo die nächste Apotheke ist?
translations.en: Do you know where the nearest pharmacy is?
translations.fr: Savez-vous où se trouve la pharmacie la plus proche ?

examples.text: Até onde eu sei, essa função não existe.

translations.de: Soweit ich weiß, gibt es eine solche Funktion nicht.
translations.en: As far as I know, such a function doesn't exist.
translations.fr: Autant que je sache, une telle fonction n'existe pas.

more.definition: where; wherever (in or at what place; in or at a/any/the place that, in what situation); where (the place in or at which)
more.etymology: Latin *cundeder. Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese onde, from Latin unde (“whence”). Compare Spanish donde.

senses.gloss: o lugar em que; o lugar no qual

examples.text: Nós aprendemos a nossa lição.

translations.de: Wir haben unsere Lektion gelernt.
translations.en: We've learned our lesson.
translations.fr: Nous avons appris notre leçon.

examples.text: Todos nós aprendemos idiomas. E Tatoeba é nosso grande professor.

translations.de: Wir alle lernen Sprachen. Und Tatoeba ist unsere großartige Lehrerin.
translations.en: We all learn languages. And Tatoeba is our great teacher.
translations.fr: Nous apprenons tous des langues. Et Tatoeba est notre excellent professeur.

examples.text: Ânimo, pois, ó bravos, nossos lares estão à vossa espera.

translations.de: Nur Mut, ihr Tapferen, unsere Heimat erwartet euch.
translations.en: Take heart, then, brave ones, our homes await you.
translations.fr: Courage, donc, braves gens, nos foyers vous attendent.

examples.text: O Tom pediu nossa ajuda.

translations.de: Tom bat um unsere Hilfe.
translations.en: Tom asked for our help.
translations.fr: Tom a demandé notre aide.

more.definition: our (belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of us, excluding the person(s) being addressed); our (belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of us, including the person(s) being addressed); our (belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese nosso, from Latin nostrum, from Proto-Italic *nosteros.

examples.text: Ele sempre estará em nossos corações.

translations.de: Er wird immer in unseren Herzen sein.
translations.en: He will forever be in our hearts.
translations.fr: Il demeurera à jamais dans nos cœurs.

examples.text: Nossa mestra é também nossa amiga e nossa irmã.

translations.de: Unsere Lehrerin ist zugleich unsere Freundin und unsere Schwester.
translations.en: Our teacher is also our friend and our sister.
translations.fr: Notre maîtresse est aussi notre amie et notre sœur.

examples.text: Bem-vinda ao nosso restaurante!

translations.de: Willkommen in unserem Restaurant!
translations.en: Welcome to our restaurant!
translations.fr: Bienvenue dans notre restaurant !

examples.text: Ao estudar idiomas, nós abrimos novas janelas por onde espreitam nossas almas.

translations.de: Durch das Erlernen von Sprachen öffnen wir neue Fenster, durch die unsere Seele blicken kann.
translations.en: By studying languages, we open new windows through which our souls peek.
translations.fr: En étudiant les langues, nous ouvrons de nouvelles fenêtres à travers lesquelles nos âmes regardent.

more.definition: ours (used substantively, with an implied noun)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese nosso, from Latin nostrum, from Proto-Italic *nosteros.

examples.text: Ele viverá para sempre em nossos corações.

translations.de: Er wird in unseren Herzen immer weiterleben.
translations.en: He will live forever in our hearts.
translations.fr: Il survivra à jamais dans nos cœurs.

examples.text: Há muitas estrelas maiores que o nosso Sol.

translations.de: Es gibt viele Sterne, die größer als unsere Sonne sind.
translations.en: There are many stars larger than our sun.
translations.fr: Il y a beaucoup d'étoiles plus grandes que notre Soleil.

examples.text: Eu sou o mais alto da nossa classe.

translations.de: Ich bin der Größte in meiner Klasse.
translations.en: I am the tallest in our class.
translations.fr: Je suis le plus grand de notre classe.

examples.text: Os revisores melhoram muito a qualidade de nossas frases.

translations.de: Korrektoren verbessern die Qualität unserer Sätze erheblich.
translations.en: Proofreaders greatly improve the quality of our sentences.
translations.fr: Les relecteurs améliorent grandement la qualité de nos phrases.

more.definition: ours (that or those belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of us, excluding the person(s) being addressed); ours (that or those belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of us, including the person(s) being addressed); ours (that or those belonging to, associated with, related to, or in the possession of any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese nosso, from Latin nostrum, from Proto-Italic *nosteros.

examples.text: Ele brinca fingindo ser outra pessoa.

translations.de: Er scherzt und gibt sich als jemand anderes aus.
translations.en: He jokes around, pretending to be someone else.
translations.fr: Il plaisante en faisant semblant d'être quelqu'un d'autre.

examples.text: Ajudar os outros nunca é desperdício de tempo.

translations.de: Anderen zu helfen ist nie eine Zeitverschwendung.
translations.en: Helping others is never a waste of time.
translations.fr: Aider les autres n'est jamais une perte de temps.

examples.text: Você fala outro idioma sem ser o inglês?

translations.de: Sprechen Sie eine andere Sprache ausser Englisch?
translations.en: Can you speak a language other than English?
translations.fr: Peux-tu parler une autre langue que l'anglais ?

examples.text: No xadrez, assim como em outras modalidades esportivas, ninguém é imbatível.

translations.de: Im Schach wie in anderen Sportarten ist niemand unschlagbar.
translations.en: At chess, as at other sports, no one is unbeatable.
translations.fr: Aux échecs, comme dans d'autres sports, personne n'est imbattable.

more.definition: other (not the one previously referred to); another (one more); another (not the same)
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-der. Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese outro, from Latin alterum.

examples.text: Sem demora, outra porta se abrirá.

translations.de: Unverzüglich wird sich eine weitere Tür öffnen.
translations.en: Without delay, another door will open.
translations.fr: Sans tarder, une autre porte s'ouvrira.

examples.text: Alguns eram fazendeiros, outros eram caçadores.

translations.de: Die einen waren Bauern; die anderen waren Jäger.
translations.en: Some were farmers, some were hunters.
translations.fr: Certains étaient des fermiers, certains des chasseurs.

examples.text: Não se esqueçam de conversar um com o outro.

translations.de: Vergesst nicht, miteinander zu reden.
translations.en: Don't forget to talk to each other.
translations.fr: N'oubliez pas de vous parler.

examples.text: Não consigo pensar de outra maneira.

translations.de: Anders kann ich nicht denken.
translations.en: I cannot think any other way.
translations.fr: Je n'arrive pas à penser d'une autre façon.

more.definition: other one (not the one previously referred to); another (one more); another (not the same)
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-der. Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese outro, from Latin alterum.

senses.gloss: que é diferente da pessoa ou da coisa que foi mencionada; que não é o mesmo; diverso, diferente

examples.text: Não há nada de errado em envelhecer.

translations.de: Es ist nichts Falsches daran, alt zu werden.
translations.en: There's nothing wrong with growing old.
translations.fr: Il n'y a pas de mal à vieillir.

examples.text: Ele não enxerga nada sem os óculos.

translations.de: Er sieht nichts ohne seine Brille.
translations.en: He cannot see anything without his glasses.
translations.fr: Il ne voit rien sans ses lunettes.

examples.text: A minha vida sem você não vale nada.

translations.de: Ohne dich ist mein Leben wertlos.
translations.en: My life without you is worth nothing.
translations.fr: Ma vie n'a aucun sens sans toi.

examples.text: Ele não sabe vender nada. Só sabe comprar.

translations.de: Er weiß nicht, wie man etwas verkauft. Er weiß nur, wie man kauft.
translations.en: He doesn't know how to sell anything. He only knows how to buy.
translations.fr: Il ne sait rien vendre. Il sait seulement acheter.

more.definition: to no extent; in no way; not at all; emphasises that a statement is false
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese nada, from Latin (nūlla rēs) nāta (literally “no born thing, not a thing born”).

examples.text: Não há nada de novo sob o Sol.

translations.de: Es gibt nichts Neues unter der Sonne.
translations.en: There is nothing new under the sun.
translations.fr: Il n'y a rien de nouveau sous le soleil.

examples.text: Não tem mais nada para comer.

translations.de: Es ist nichts mehr zu essen da.
translations.en: There is nothing left to eat.
translations.fr: Il n'y a plus rien à manger.

examples.text: Não tenho mais nada a adicionar.

translations.de: Ich habe dem nichts mehr hinzuzufügen.
translations.en: I have nothing else to add to that.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien d'autre à ajouter.

examples.text: Você não disse nada para ele?

translations.de: Du hast ihm nichts gesagt?
translations.en: You didn't tell him anything?
translations.fr: Tu ne lui as rien dit ?

more.definition: nothingness (the state of not existing); the void (the vacuum of space); a very small amount
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese nada, from Latin (nūlla rēs) nāta (literally “no born thing, not a thing born”).

examples.text: Estou entediado. Não tenho nada interessante para fazer.

translations.de: Mir ist langweilig. Ich habe nichts Interessantes zu tun.
translations.en: I'm bored. I have nothing interesting to do.
translations.fr: Je m'ennuie. Je n'ai rien d'intéressant à faire.

examples.text: Espero por nada. Não temo nada. Estou livre.

translations.de: Ich erhoffe nichts. Ich fürchte nichts. Ich bin frei.
translations.en: I hope for nothing. I fear nothing. I am free.
translations.fr: Je n'espère rien, je ne crains rien, je suis libre.

examples.text: Eu não tenho nada na geladeira.

translations.de: Ich habe nichts in meinem Kühlschrank.
translations.en: I've got nothing in my fridge.
translations.fr: Je n'ai rien dans mon frigo.

examples.text: Vocês não estão entendendo absolutamente nada.

translations.de: Sie verstehen überhaupt nichts.
translations.en: You don't understand anything at all.
translations.fr: Vous ne comprenez rien du tout.

more.definition: nothing (not any thing; no thing)
idioms: e na bundinha não vai nada?
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese nada, from Latin (nūlla rēs) nāta (literally “no born thing, not a thing born”).

examples.text: Ele estará de volta em dez minutos.

translations.de: Er ist in zehn Minuten zurück.
translations.en: He will be back in ten minutes.
translations.fr: Il sera de retour dans dix minutes.

examples.text: Vivo a sonhar que estás voltando para mim.

translations.de: Ich träume immer wieder davon, dass du zu mir zurückkommst.
translations.en: I keep dreaming that you're coming back to me.
translations.fr: Je continue de rêver que tu reviens vers moi.

examples.text: Por que vocês não voltam para a cidade?

translations.de: Warum geht ihr nicht zurück in die Stadt?
translations.en: Why don't you go back to the city?
translations.fr: Pourquoi ne retournez-vous pas en ville ?

examples.text: Haaland voltou a marcar cinco gols em uma partida.

translations.de: Haaland erzielte erneut fünf Tore in einem Spiel.
translations.en: Haaland scored five goals in one match again.
translations.fr: Haaland a de nouveau marqué cinq buts en un seul match.

more.definition: to return; to come back; to return (to reach a previous state); to turn (to adjust something in a direction)
more.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *welH-der. Latin volvereder. Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese voltar, from Vulgar Latin *vol(vi)tāre, from Latin volvere.

examples.text: Eu penso muito na minha família.

translations.de: Ich denke oft an meine Familie.
translations.en: I often think of my family.
translations.fr: Je pense souvent à ma famille.

examples.text: O que você pensa sobre este livro?

translations.de: Was denkst du über dieses Buch?
translations.en: What do you think about this book?
translations.fr: Que penses-tu de ce livre ?

examples.text: A mulher observa e o homem pensa.

translations.de: Die Frau beobachtet und der Mann denkt.
translations.en: The woman observes and the man thinks.
translations.fr: La femme observe et l'homme raisonne.

examples.text: Eu não sei o que ela está pensando.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, was sie denkt.
translations.en: I don't know what she's thinking.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas à quoi elle pense.

examples.text: Já não penso na morte, é preciso cantar.

translations.de: Ich denke nicht mehr an den Tod, ich muss singen.
translations.en: I don't think about death anymore, I have to sing.
translations.fr: Je ne pense plus à la mort, je dois chanter.

examples.text: Tom pensou que Mary estivesse dormindo.

translations.de: Tom dachte, dass Maria schläft.
translations.en: Tom thought that Mary was asleep.
translations.fr: Tom pensait que Mary était endormie.

more.definition: to think (communicate to oneself in one’s mind); to conceive, intend
more.etymology: Inherited from Latin pēnsāre. Doublet of pesar.

examples.text: Ele comprou um novo dicionário para mim.

translations.de: Er hat mir ein neues Wörterbuch gekauft.
translations.en: He bought me a new dictionary.
translations.fr: Il m'a acheté un nouveau dictionnaire.

examples.text: Raro tesouro para mim era a amizade dela.

translations.de: Ein seltener Schatz für mich war ihre Freundschaft.
translations.en: Her friendship was a rare treasure to me.
translations.fr: Un trésor rare pour moi était son amitié.

examples.text: Maria, tua amizade é muito importante para mim.

translations.de: Marie, deine Freundschaft ist mir sehr wichtig.
translations.en: Mary, your friendship is very important to me.
translations.fr: Marie, ton amitié est très importante pour moi.

examples.text: Acho que ela não se lembra de mim.

translations.de: Ich glaube, sie erinnert sich nicht an mich.
translations.en: I guess she doesn't remember me.
translations.fr: Je pense qu'elle ne se souvient pas de moi.

more.definition: first-person singular prepositional pronoun
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese mi, min from Latin mihi, from Proto-Indo-European *méǵʰye, dative of *éǵh₂ (“I”).

examples.text: Obrigado pela sopa.

translations.de: Danke für die Suppe!
translations.en: Thanks for the soup.
translations.fr: Merci pour la soupe.

examples.text: Obrigada a ambos.

translations.de: Danke, ihr zwei!
translations.en: Thanks to both of you.
translations.fr: Merci à vous deux.

examples.text: Obrigado a ambas.

translations.de: Danke, ihr zwei!
translations.en: Thanks to both of you.
translations.fr: Merci à vous deux.

examples.text: Obrigado a ambos.

translations.de: Danke, ihr zwei!
translations.en: Thanks to both of you.
translations.fr: Merci à vous deux.

more.definition: obligatory; mandatory (required or commanded by authority); grateful, thankful
more.etymology: Semi-learned borrowing from Latin obligātus (“obliged”), past participle of obligō (“to bind in obligation”).

examples.text: Estou bem, obrigado por perguntar.

translations.de: Es geht mir gut. Danke der Nachfrage!
translations.en: I'm fine, thanks for asking.
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci de me le demander !

examples.text: Eu estou bem, obrigado.

translations.de: Es geht mir gut, danke.
translations.en: I am fine, thank you.
translations.fr: Je vais bien, merci.

examples.text: Muito bem, obrigado.

translations.de: Sehr gut, danke.
translations.en: Very good, thank you.
translations.fr: Très bien, merci.

examples.text: Obrigado, mas infelizmente não posso.

translations.de: Danke, aber leider kann ich nicht.
translations.en: Thank you, but unfortunately I can't.
translations.fr: Merci, mais malheureusement je ne peux pas.

more.definition: thanks; thank you
more.etymology: Semi-learned borrowing from Latin obligātus (“obliged”), past participle of obligō (“to bind in obligation”).

senses.gloss: expressa agradecimento da parte de uma pessoa de sexo masculino

examples.text: Obrigado por virem, pessoal! Vejo vocês na próxima aula!

translations.de: Danke, dass ihr gekommen seid! Bis zum nächsten Mal!
translations.en: Thanks for coming, guys! I'll see you next class!
translations.fr: Merci à tous d'être venus ! On se revoit au prochain cours !

examples.text: Obrigada a ambas.

translations.de: Danke, ihr zwei!
translations.en: Thanks to both of you.
translations.fr: Merci à vous deux.

examples.text: Obrigado pelo seu comentário.

translations.de: Danke für Ihren Kommentar.
translations.en: Thank you for your comment.
translations.fr: Merci pour votre commentaire.

examples.text: Obrigado por sua explicação.

translations.de: Danke für Ihre Erklärung.
translations.en: Thanks for your explanation.
translations.fr: Merci pour ton explication.

more.definition: someone bound by a legal obligation; a thank you (instance of expressing gratitude)
more.etymology: Semi-learned borrowing from Latin obligātus (“obliged”), past participle of obligō (“to bind in obligation”).

examples.text: Eu estou lendo um livro sobre animais.

translations.de: Ich lese ein Buch über Tiere.
translations.en: I am reading a book about animals.
translations.fr: Je lis un livre sur les animaux.

examples.text: A caixa está sobre a mesa.

translations.de: Die Kiste steht auf dem Tisch.
translations.en: The box is on the table.
translations.fr: La boîte est sur la table.

examples.text: O arco-íris lança chuva sobre a terra.

translations.de: Der Regenbogen wirft Regen auf die Erde.
translations.en: The rainbow casts rain on the earth.
translations.fr: L'arc-en-ciel jette la pluie sur la terre.

examples.text: Há uma ponte de corda sobre o rio.

translations.de: Über den Fluss führt eine Seilbrücke.
translations.en: There's a rope bridge over the river.
translations.fr: Il y a un pont de corde sur la rivière.

more.etymology: Do latim super⁽ˡᵃ⁾.

examples.text: Esparta aspirava à hegemonia sobre toda a Grécia.

translations.de: Sparta strebte nach der Hegemonie über ganz Griechenland.
translations.en: Sparta aspired to hegemony over all of Greece.
translations.fr: Sparte aspirait à l’hégémonie sur toute la Grèce.

examples.text: Neste momento, estou escrevendo uma frase sobre o amor.

translations.de: Ich schreibe gerade einen Satz über die Liebe.
translations.en: Right now, I'm writing a sentence about love.
translations.fr: En ce moment, j'écris une phrase sur l'amour.

examples.text: Eu pensei muito sobre isso.

translations.de: Ich habe viel darüber nachgedacht.
translations.en: I thought about it a lot.
translations.fr: J'y ai beaucoup pensé.

examples.text: A influência da TV sobre a sociedade é grande.

translations.de: Der Einfluss des Fernsehens auf die Gesellschaft ist groß.
translations.en: The influence of TV on society is great.
translations.fr: L'influence de la TV sur la société est grande.

more.definition: on; atop; on top of (located on the top surface of); over; above (in or through the space above); about; concerning (on the subject of)
idioms: estar um astro sobre o horizonte
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese sobre, from Latin super, from *eks-uper, which consists of Proto-Indo-European *eḱs (“out of”) and *uperi. Doublet of the borrowed super. Cognate to Spanish sobre, French sur, Ancient Greek ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”) and English over, super and sur-.

senses.gloss: elemento formador de adjuntos adverbiais que exprimem a ideia de:

examples.text: Na França, temos de deixar uma gorjeta?

translations.de: Müssen wir in Frankreich ein Trinkgeld hinterlassen?
translations.en: Do we have to leave a tip in France?
translations.fr: Doit-on laisser un pourboire en France ?

examples.text: Eu amo alguém que sem motivo me deixou.

translations.de: Ich liebe jemanden, die mich ohne Grund verlassen hat.
translations.en: I love someone who left me for no reason.
translations.fr: J'aime quelqu'un qui m'a quitté sans raison.

examples.text: Olhos nos olhos, nos deixamos fascinar.

translations.de: Auge in Auge, lassen wir uns faszinieren.
translations.en: Eyes in eyes, we let ourselves be fascinated.
translations.fr: Les yeux dans les yeux, on se laisse fasciner.

examples.text: Ele não dá sinais de que se deixe intimidar.

translations.de: Er zeigt keine Anzeichen von Einschüchterung.
translations.en: He shows no signs of being intimidated.
translations.fr: Il ne montre aucun signe d’intimidation.

more.definition: to leave; to exit (to go out of or away from a place); to leave (to refrain from taking); to leave, to leave behind (to cause to exist after its occurrence)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese leixar, from Latin laxāre (“to extend; to lighten; to relax; to release”), from laxus (“loose”). Doublet of the borrowed laxar. Compare Galician deixar, Asturian dexar, and Spanish dejar, all also undergoing the shift of initial -l- to -d-. It may have been influenced by the preposition de or come from contraction of a Late Latin *dēlaxāre.

examples.text: Não sei porque estou aqui.

translations.de: Ich weiß nicht, wieso ich hier bin.
translations.en: I don't know why I'm here.
translations.fr: Je ne sais pas pourquoi je suis ici.

examples.text: Eu sei que nada sei, porque não sei quem sou.

translations.de: Ich weiß, dass ich nichts weiß, weil ich nicht weiß, wer ich bin.
translations.en: I know that I know nothing, because I do not know who I am.
translations.fr: Je sais que je ne sais rien, car je ne sais pas qui je suis.

examples.text: Eu tenho medo das baratas, porque são nojentas e feias.

translations.de: Ich habe Angst vor Kakerlaken, denn sie sind ekelhaft und hässlich.
translations.en: I'm afraid of cockroaches, because they are disgusting and ugly.
translations.fr: J'ai peur des cafards, parce qu'ils sont dégoûtants et laids.

examples.text: O esforço valeu a pena porque eu passei no teste.

translations.de: Die Anstrengung war die Mühe wert, da ich den Test bestanden habe.
translations.en: The hard work was worthwhile because I passed the exam.
translations.fr: L'effort en valait la peine car j'ai réussi le test.

more.definition: European Portuguese standard spelling of por que; pre-reform spelling (used until 1943) of por que; now a common misspelling
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese porque, from Vulgar Latin [Term?]. By surface analysis, univerbation of por (“for”) + que (“that”). Doublet of por que. Cognate with Galician and Spanish porque, Catalan perquè, French parce que and Italian perché.

examples.text: Eu caí porque desci muito rápido.

translations.de: Ich bin gefallen, weil ich zu schnell runtergegangen bin.
translations.en: I fell because I went down too fast.
translations.fr: Je suis tombé parce que je suis descendu trop vite.

examples.text: Estou muito feliz porque meu time ganhou o campeonato.

translations.de: Ich freue mich sehr, dass meine Mannschaft die Meisterschaft gewonnen hat.
translations.en: I'm really happy because my team won the championship.
translations.fr: Je suis très heureux car mon équipe a remporté le championnat.

examples.text: Esse peixe não pode ver porque não tem olhos.

translations.de: Dieser Fisch kann nicht sehen, weil er keine Augen hat.
translations.en: That fish cannot see because he does not have eyes.
translations.fr: Ce poisson ne peut pas voir car il n'a pas d'yeux.

examples.text: Compre um bom calçado porque andaremos muito nesta caminhada.

translations.de: Kaufen Sie gute Schuhe, denn wir werden auf dieser Wanderung viel spazieren gehen.
translations.en: Buy some good shoes because we will be walking a lot on this hike.
translations.fr: Achète de bonnes chaussures parce que nous marcherons beaucoup pendant cette randonnée.

more.definition: because (introduces a reason for that described in the previous clause); because (introduces an explanation to a claim in the previous clause)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese porque, from Vulgar Latin [Term?]. By surface analysis, univerbation of por (“for”) + que (“that”). Doublet of por que. Cognate with Galician and Spanish porque, Catalan perquè, French parce que and Italian perché.

senses.gloss: causa, motivo ou razão da ação contida na oração principal; como, visto que, já que

examples.text: Estou bebendo água porque estou com sede.

translations.de: Ich trinke Wasser, weil ich durstig bin.
translations.en: I'm drinking water because I'm thirsty.
translations.fr: Je bois de l'eau parce que j'ai soif.

examples.text: Eles eram felizes porque se amavam.

translations.de: Sie waren glücklich, weil sie einander liebten.
translations.en: They were happy because they loved each other.
translations.fr: Ils étaient heureux car ils s'aimaient.

examples.text: Nós éramos felizes porque nos amávamos.

translations.de: Wir waren glücklich, weil wir einander liebten.
translations.en: We were happy because we loved each other.
translations.fr: Nous étions heureux parce que nous nous aimions.

examples.text: Quero ser médico porque meu pai era médico.

translations.de: Ich möchte Arzt werden, weil mein Vater Arzt war.
translations.en: I want to be a doctor because my father was a doctor.
translations.fr: Je veux devenir médecin parce que mon père était médecin.

more.etymology: (Morfologia) por + que.

senses.gloss: introduz orações interrogativas; por que razão, por que motivo

examples.text: O que você come no café da manhã?

translations.de: Was isst du zum Frühstück?
translations.en: What do you eat for breakfast?
translations.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu manges au petit-déjeuner ?

examples.text: Nós comemos em um restaurante ontem.

translations.de: Wir haben gestern im Restaurant gegessen.
translations.en: We ate at a restaurant yesterday.
translations.fr: Nous avons mangé au restaurant hier.

examples.text: Se não têm pão, que comam brioches.

translations.de: Wenn sie kein Brot haben, dann sollen sie eben Kuchen essen!
translations.en: If they don't have bread, let them eat cake.
translations.fr: S’ils n’ont pas de pain, qu’ils mangent de la brioche !

examples.text: Eu estou cansado de comer fast-food.

translations.de: Ich habe es satt, Fastfood zu essen.
translations.en: I'm tired of eating fast food.
translations.fr: J'en ai marre de manger du fast-food.

examples.text: Por que comemos peru na ceia de Natal?

translations.de: Warum essen wir am Weihnachtsessen Truthahn?
translations.en: Why do we eat turkey for Christmas dinner?
translations.fr: Pourquoi mange-t-on de la dinde pour le dîner de Noël ?

examples.text: Netuno, o senhor dos mares, não come peixe.

translations.de: Neptun, der Herr der Meere, isst keinen Fisch.
translations.en: Neptune, the lord of the seas, does not eat fish.
translations.fr: Neptune, le seigneur des mers, ne mange pas de poisson.

more.definition: to consume meals; to consume a specific food; to eat some
idioms: comer o pão que o diabo amassou
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese comer, from Vulgar Latin *comēre, restructuring of Latin comedere. Cognate with Galician, Mirandese, Asturian, and Spanish comer and Mirandese quemer.

examples.text: Eu podia sentir a emoção crescendo no ar.

translations.de: Ich konnte die wachsende Aufregung in der Luft spüren.
translations.en: I could feel the excitement building in the air.
translations.fr: Je sentais l'excitation monter dans l'air.

examples.text: Eu sinto ainda muita falta dela.

translations.de: Ich vermisse sie immer noch sehr.
translations.en: I still miss her very much.
translations.fr: Elle me manque encore terriblement.

examples.text: Ontem dormi mal e hoje estou me sentindo fraco.

translations.de: Ich habe gestern schlecht geschlafen und fühle mich heute schwach.
translations.en: I didn't sleep well last night, and today I'm feeling weak.
translations.fr: Hier, j'ai mal dormi et aujourd'hui, je me sens faible.

examples.text: Ninguém entende o que eu sinto.

translations.de: Niemand versteht, was ich fühle.
translations.en: No one understands how I feel.
translations.fr: Personne ne comprend ce que je ressens.

more.definition: to sense; to feel (to perceive by means of biological senses); to feel (to feel with the skin or hands); to feel (to experience an emotion or feeling [noun])
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese sentir, from Latin sentīre, from Proto-Indo-European *sent- (“to head for, go”).

examples.text: Roma não se fez em um dia.

translations.de: Rom wurde nicht in einem Tage erbaut.
translations.en: Rome wasn't built in a day.
translations.fr: Rome ne s'est pas faite en un jour.

examples.text: Nestes últimos dias, tenho trabalhado muito.

translations.de: Ich habe die letzten Tage sehr viel gearbeitet.
translations.en: I've been working a lot these past few days.
translations.fr: J'ai beaucoup travaillé ces derniers jours.

examples.text: Um dia tem vinte e quatro horas.

translations.de: Ein Tag hat vierundzwanzig Stunden.
translations.en: A day has twenty-four hours.
translations.fr: Un jour compte vingt-quatre heures.

examples.text: Roma não foi feita em um dia.

translations.de: Rom wurde nicht in einem Tage erbaut.
translations.en: Rome was not built in a day.
translations.fr: Rome ne s'est pas faite en un jour.

more.definition: period between sunrise and sunset; period from midnight to the following midnight; period of 24 hours
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese dia, from Vulgar Latin *dia, first-declension reshaping of Classical Latin diēs, reformed from the accusative diem, from Proto-Italic *djēm, the accusative of *djous (“day, sky”), from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws (“heaven, sky”). Distantly related to Deus, Zeus and Jove.

senses.gloss: espaço de tempo correspondente à rotação da Terra, que equivale a 23 horas, 56 minutos e 4 segundos

examples.text: O tempo vai melhorar em breve.

translations.de: Das Wetter wird sich bald bessern.
translations.en: The weather will clear up soon.
translations.fr: Le temps va bientôt s'éclaircir.

examples.text: O tempo que passou não volta nunca mais.

translations.de: Die vergangene Zeit wird nie wiederkehren.
translations.en: The time that has passed will never come back.
translations.fr: Le temps qui est passé ne reviendra jamais.

examples.text: Por que falas ao vento? Estás perdendo tempo!

translations.de: Warum sprichst du mit dem Wind? Du verschwendest Zeit!
translations.en: Why do you speak to the wind? You're wasting time!
translations.fr: Pourquoi parlez-vous au vent ? Vous perdez du temps !

examples.text: Eu quero passar tempo junto contigo.

translations.de: Ich will Zeit mit dir verbringen.
translations.en: I want to spend time with you.
translations.fr: Je veux passer du temps avec toi.

more.definition: time out (call for a time-out)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese tempo, from Latin tempus (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *tempos (“stretch”), from the root *temp- (“to stretch, string”).

examples.text: Já é tempo de visitar os lírios.

translations.de: Es ist Zeit, die Lilien zu besuchen.
translations.en: It's time to visit the lilies.
translations.fr: Il est temps d'aller admirer les lys.

examples.text: O mau tempo não dura para sempre.

translations.de: Schlechtes Wetter dauert nicht ewig.
translations.en: Bad weather won't last forever.
translations.fr: Le mauvais temps ne dure pas éternellement.

examples.text: A escola é uma perda de tempo.

translations.de: Schule ist Zeitverschwendung.
translations.en: School is a waste of time.
translations.fr: L'école est une perte de temps.

examples.text: A verdade é a filha do tempo.

translations.de: Wahrheit ist eine Tochter der Zeit.
translations.en: Truth is the daughter of time.
translations.fr: La vérité est la fille du temps.

more.definition: time (the progression from the present into the future); time (quantity of availability of duration); a duration of time, especially a long one
idioms: não ter tempo para se coçar
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese tempo, from Latin tempus (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *tempos (“stretch”), from the root *temp- (“to stretch, string”).

senses.gloss: continuum linear não-espacial no qual os eventos se sucedem irreversivelmente

examples.text: Eu gosto dessa música.

translations.de: Ich mag dieses Lied.
translations.en: I like this song.
translations.fr: J'aime cette chanson.

examples.text: Ela gosta de ler à noite.

translations.de: Sie liest abends gern.
translations.en: She likes to read in the evening.
translations.fr: Elle aime lire le soir.

examples.text: Eu gostaria de convidar você para jantar.

translations.de: Ich möchte dich zum Abendessen einladen.
translations.en: I would like to invite you to dinner.
translations.fr: J'aimerais t'inviter à dîner.

examples.text: Ela gosta de cozinhar para sua família.

translations.de: Sie kocht gerne für ihre Familie.
translations.en: She likes to cook for her family.
translations.fr: Elle aime cuisiner pour sa famille.

examples.text: Ele perguntou se eu gostava de comida chinesa.

translations.de: Er fragte, ob ich chinesisches Essen möge.
translations.en: He asked if I liked Chinese food.
translations.fr: Il a demandé si j'aimais la nourriture chinoise.

examples.text: Minha irmã iria gostar desse vestido, ela adora vermelho.

translations.de: Dieses Kleid würde meiner Schwester gefallen, sie liebt Rot.
translations.en: My sister would like this dress; she loves red.
translations.fr: Cette robe plairait à ma sœur, elle adore le rouge.

more.definition: to like
collocations: gostar muito de — to like a lot
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese gostar, from Latin gustāre. Compare Spanish gustar.

examples.text: Tenho vontade de beijá-la mil vezes.

translations.de: Ich möchte sie tausend Mal küssen.
translations.en: I want to kiss her a thousand times.
translations.fr: J'ai envie de l'embrasser mille fois.

examples.text: Ela o visitava uma vez por ano.

translations.de: Sie besuchte ihn einmal im Jahr.
translations.en: She visited him once a year.
translations.fr: Elle lui rendait visite une fois par an.

examples.text: Eu adivinho nove em cada dez vezes.

translations.de: Ich rate in neun von zehn Fällen richtig.
translations.en: I guess right nine times out of ten.
translations.fr: Je devine juste neuf fois sur dix.

examples.text: Nós dois nadamos juntos uma vez por semana.

translations.de: Wir schwimmen einmal pro Woche zusammen.
translations.en: The two of us swim together once a week.
translations.fr: Nous allons nager ensemble une fois par semaine.

more.definition: time; occasion; move (chance to use something shared in sequence with others); turn; move (one’s chance to make a move in a game having two or more players)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese vez (displacing vegada), from Latin vicis (“change, alternation”), from Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to wind, bend”).

examples.text: O Tom trabalha das nove às cinco.

translations.de: Tom arbeitet von neun bis fünf.
translations.en: Tom works from nine to five.
translations.fr: Tom travaille de 9h à 17h.

examples.text: Este mês, meu filho está trabalhando em casa.

translations.de: Diesen Monat arbeitet mein Sohn von zu Hause aus.
translations.en: This month, my son is working from home.
translations.fr: Ce mois-ci, mon fils travaille à la maison.

examples.text: Como você consegue trabalhar e estudar?

translations.de: Wie schaffen Sie es, zu arbeiten und zu studieren?
translations.en: How do you manage to work and study?
translations.fr: Comment faites-vous pour travailler et étudier ?

examples.text: Eu trabalhei durante trinta anos no Banco do Brasil.

translations.de: Ich habe dreißig Jahre lang bei der Banco do Brasil gearbeitet.
translations.en: I worked at Banco do Brasil for thirty years.
translations.fr: J'ai travaillé pendant trente ans à la Banque du Brésil.

more.definition: to work (to do a specific task)
idioms: trabalhar como um burro de carga
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese traballar, from Vulgar Latin *tripāliāre (“torment”), derived from Late Latin tripālium (“torture instrument”). Compare Galician traballar, Spanish trabajar. By surface analysis, trabalho + -ar.

senses.gloss: realizar alguma atividade em troca de remuneração

examples.text: De várias maneiras algo pode ser dito em Toki Pona.

translations.de: In Toki Pona kann man etwas auf verschiedene Weisen sagen.
translations.en: In many ways, something can be said in Toki Pona.
translations.fr: De bien des façons, on peut dire la même chose à toki pona.

examples.text: Tom está comendo algo.

translations.de: Tom isst etwas.
translations.en: Tom is eating something.
translations.fr: Tom mange quelque chose.

examples.text: Posso dizer algo?

translations.de: Darf ich etwas sagen?
translations.en: May I say something?
translations.fr: Puis-je dire quelque chose ?

examples.text: O sono é algo semelhante à morte. Morrer é, simplesmente, não acordar.

translations.de: Schlaf ist so etwas wie der Tod. Sterben bedeutet schlicht und einfach, nicht mehr aufzuwachen.
translations.en: Sleep is something akin to death. To die is, simply, not to wake up.
translations.fr: Le sommeil est une sorte de mort. Mourir, c'est tout simplement ne pas se réveiller.

more.definition: rather, somewhat
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese algo, from Latin aliquod (“some; a few”).

examples.text: A vida sem livros é algo inimaginável.

translations.de: Ein Leben ohne Bücher ist unvorstellbar.
translations.en: Life without books is unimaginable.
translations.fr: La vie sans livre est inimaginable.

examples.text: Tenho a impressão de que algo está faltando.

translations.de: Ich habe den Eindruck, dass etwas fehlt.
translations.en: I have a feeling that something is missing.
translations.fr: J'ai l'impression qu'il manque quelque chose.

examples.text: Avistava-se ao longe algo parecido com uma choça.

translations.de: In der Ferne war so etwas wie eine Hütte zu sehen.
translations.en: Something like a hut could be seen in the distance.
translations.fr: On apercevait au loin quelque chose qui ressemblait à une cabane.

examples.text: Tom fez algo muito estúpido.

translations.de: Tom hat etwas sehr Dummes getan.
translations.en: Tom did something very stupid.
translations.fr: Tom fit quelque chose de très stupide.

more.definition: something (unspecified object)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese algo, from Latin aliquod (“some; a few”).

examples.text: A música tem o poder de tranquilizar até as feras.

translations.de: Musik hat die Macht, sogar Tiere zu beruhigen.
translations.en: Music has a charm that soothes even the savage's breast.
translations.fr: La musique a le pouvoir de calmer même les bêtes.

examples.text: Conto sempre até dez antes de fazer qualquer coisa quando me zango.

translations.de: Ich zähle immer bis zehn, bevor ich irgendetwas tue, wenn ich wütend bin.
translations.en: I always count to ten before doing anything when I get angry.
translations.fr: Je compte toujours jusqu'à dix avant de faire quoi que ce soit quand je me mets en colère.

examples.text: Todo o universo está interligado. A consciência até nos átomos se encontra.

translations.de: Das gesamte Universum ist miteinander verbunden. Selbst in den Atomen findet sich Bewusstsein.
translations.en: The entire universe is interconnected. Consciousness is found even in atoms.
translations.fr: L'univers entier est interconnecté. La conscience se trouve même dans les atomes.

examples.text: O despotismo e a prepotência mais absurda punem até supremas cortes estrangeiras.

translations.de: Willkür und die absurdeste Arroganz bestrafen sogar ausländische Oberste Gerichte.
translations.en: Despotism and the most absurd arrogance punish even supreme foreign courts.
translations.fr: Le despotisme et l'arrogance les plus absurdes punissent même les cours suprêmes étrangères.

more.definition: even (implying an extreme example in the case mentioned); including (introducing one or more parts of the group or topic just mentioned); very much; to a great extent (implies a continuation)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese até, ata of uncertain origin. Possibly from Arabic حَتَّى (ḥattā), Latin ad ista (“to this”) or Latin ad tenus (“as far as”) (>"ad tenes"), which explain the large number of mediaeval variants (atrõe, atée, atrõo, attaa, atẽe, atães, tẽe and so on). However, considering the rarity of tenus, possibly from Latin intrā. Compare Spanish hasta, Leonese ata, Asturian ta.

examples.text: Te acompanho até a estação.

translations.de: Ich begleite dich zum Bahnhof.
translations.en: I will go along with you as far as the station.
translations.fr: Je vais t'accompagner jusqu'à la gare.

examples.text: Contem de um até cem.

translations.de: Zählt von eins bis hundert!
translations.en: Count from one to a hundred.
translations.fr: Comptez de un à cent.

examples.text: Minha cidade é muito quente. Faz calor até no inverno.

translations.de: In meiner Stadt ist es sehr heiß. Selbst im Winter ist es heiß.
translations.en: My city is very hot. It's hot even in winter.
translations.fr: Ma ville est très chaude. Il y fait chaud même en hiver.

examples.text: O médico recomendou repouso absoluto até o fim da gravidez.

translations.de: Der Arzt empfahl absolute Bettruhe bis zum Ende der Schwangerschaft.
translations.en: The doctor recommended complete bed rest until the end of the pregnancy.
translations.fr: Le médecin a recommandé un repos complet au lit jusqu'à la fin de la grossesse.

more.definition: short for any farewell containing até (até-logo, até mais, até breve, até já): see ya; see you later; see you soon
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese até, ata of uncertain origin. Possibly from Arabic حَتَّى (ḥattā), Latin ad ista (“to this”) or Latin ad tenus (“as far as”) (>"ad tenes"), which explain the large number of mediaeval variants (atrõe, atée, atrõo, attaa, atẽe, atães, tẽe and so on). However, considering the rarity of tenus, possibly from Latin intrā. Compare Spanish hasta, Leonese ata, Asturian ta.

examples.text: Esta saudade dói e até me faz chorar.

translations.de: Diese Sehnsucht tut weh und bringt mich sogar zum Weinen.
translations.en: This longing hurts and even makes me cry.
translations.fr: Ce désir me fait mal et me fait même pleurer.

examples.text: Ninguém conseguiu até hoje jogar melhor que ele.

translations.de: Niemand hat es jemals geschafft, besser zu spielen als er.
translations.en: No one has ever managed to play better than him.
translations.fr: Personne n'a jamais réussi à jouer mieux que lui.

examples.text: Vou esperar aqui até ela vir.

translations.de: Ich werde hier warten, bis sie kommt.
translations.en: I'll wait here until she comes.
translations.fr: J'attendrai ici jusqu'à ce qu'elle vienne.

examples.text: Ele veio até aqui andando.

translations.de: Er kam zu Fuß hierher.
translations.en: He walked all the way here.
translations.fr: Il est venu ici en marchant.

more.definition: until (up to the time of something happening); by (at some point before the given time); to (all the way to a place)
idioms: água mole em pedra dura tanto bate até que fura
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese até, ata of uncertain origin. Possibly from Arabic حَتَّى (ḥattā), Latin ad ista (“to this”) or Latin ad tenus (“as far as”) (>"ad tenes"), which explain the large number of mediaeval variants (atrõe, atée, atrõo, attaa, atẽe, atães, tẽe and so on). However, considering the rarity of tenus, possibly from Latin intrā. Compare Spanish hasta, Leonese ata, Asturian ta.

examples.text: A que horas sai o próximo trem?

translations.de: Wann fährt der nächste Zug ab?
translations.en: What time does the next train leave?
translations.fr: À quelle heure part le prochain train ?

examples.text: Daqui não saio, daqui ninguém me tira.

translations.de: Ich gehe hier nicht weg, niemand kann mich hier rausholen.
translations.en: I'm not leaving here, no one can get me out of here.
translations.fr: Je ne pars pas d'ici, personne ne peut me faire sortir d'ici.

examples.text: Uma fumaça negra saiu da chaminé.

translations.de: Aus dem Schornstein kam schwarzer Rauch.
translations.en: Black smoke came out of the chimney.
translations.fr: De la fumée noire sortit de la cheminée.

examples.text: Pegue já suas coisas e saia da minha casa!

translations.de: Schnapp dir sofort deine Sachen und verschwinde aus meinem Haus!
translations.en: Grab your things and get out of my house right now!
translations.fr: Prends tes affaires tout de suite et sors de chez moi !

more.definition: to exit; to leave (go away from a certain place or situation); to get out (of); to go out (leave one’s abode to go to public places); to leave (stop being involved with)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese sair, from Latin salīre (“to leap”), from Proto-Indo-European *sl̥-ye-. Compare Galician saír and Spanish salir.

senses.gloss: passar de dentro para fora; deixar

examples.text: O olhar dela reflete águas profundas.

translations.de: Ihr Blick spiegelt tiefe Gewässer wider.
translations.en: Her gaze reflects deep waters.
translations.fr: Son regard reflète les profondeurs de l'eau.

examples.text: Inebria-se o luar buscando a luz do olhar encantador da minha amada.

translations.de: Der Mondschein berauscht sich, indem er das Licht des bezaubernden Blicks meiner Geliebten sucht.
translations.en: The moonlight intoxicates itself, seeking the light of my beloved's enchanting gaze.
translations.fr: Le clair de lune s'enivre en cherchant la lumière du regard enchanteur de ma bien-aimée.

more.definition: gaze; stare; look; glance
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese aollar, from Vulgar Latin *adoculāre, from oclus, from Latin oculus. Cognate with Galician ollar, Mirandese oulhar, Spanish aojar and Italian adocchiare.

examples.text: Você conhece o homem que está te olhando?

translations.de: Kennst du den Mann, der dich da anstarrt?
translations.en: Do you know the man who's staring at you?
translations.fr: Connais-tu l'homme qui te regarde ?

examples.text: Ela lhe olhou direto nos olhos.

translations.de: Sie schaute ihm direkt in die Augen.
translations.en: She looked him right in the eye.
translations.fr: Elle le regarda droit dans les yeux.

examples.text: A cavalo dado não se olha o dente.

translations.de: Einem geschenkten Gaul schaut man nicht ins Maul.
translations.en: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
translations.fr: À cheval donné on ne regarde pas la bride.

examples.text: Olhe os patos nadando no lago!

translations.de: Schau dir die Enten an, die im See schwimmen!
translations.en: Look at the ducks swimming in the lake!
translations.fr: Regardez les canards qui nagent dans le lac !

more.definition: to look
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese aollar, from Vulgar Latin *adoculāre, from oclus, from Latin oculus. Cognate with Galician ollar, Mirandese oulhar, Spanish aojar and Italian adocchiare.

examples.text: A torre é tão importante assim no jogo de xadrez?

translations.de: Ist der Turm im Schach so wichtig?
translations.en: Is the rook that important in the game of chess?
translations.fr: La tour est-elle si importante dans le jeu d'échecs ?

examples.text: Eu teria escrito esse texto se soubesse escrever tão bem assim.

translations.de: Ich hätte diesen Text geschrieben, wenn ich so gut schreiben könnte.
translations.en: I would have written this text if I knew how to write that well.
translations.fr: J'aurais écrit ce texte si j'avais su écrire aussi bien que ça.

examples.text: Não somos assim.

translations.de: Wir sind nicht so.
translations.en: We aren't like that.
translations.fr: Nous ne sommes pas comme ça.

examples.text: A vida é assim! Nada é fácil e nada é impossível.

translations.de: Das Leben ist so! Nichts ist einfach und nichts ist unmöglich.
translations.en: Life is like that! Nothing is easy and nothing is impossible.
translations.fr: La vie est comme ça ! Rien n'est facile et rien n'est impossible.

more.definition: full of; replete
more.etymology: From earlier assi, from Old Galician-Portuguese assi, from Late Latin ac sīc. Closely parallel to Aromanian ashi, Spanish así, Romanian așa. Compare also Catalan així, French ainsi, Italian così.

examples.text: O velho é, por assim dizer, um dicionário ambulante.

translations.de: Der alte Mann ist sozusagen ein wandelndes Wörterbuch.
translations.en: That old man is, so to speak, a walking dictionary.
translations.fr: Le vieil homme est, pour ainsi dire, un dictionnaire ambulant.

examples.text: A morte é, por assim dizer, uma espécie de baldeação.

translations.de: Der Tod ist gewissermaßen eine Art Transfer.
translations.en: Death is, so to speak, a kind of transfer.
translations.fr: La mort est, pour ainsi dire, une sorte de transfert.

examples.text: Eu mudei tanto assim?

translations.de: Habe ich mich so sehr verändert?
translations.en: Have I changed that much?
translations.fr: Ai-je tant changé ?

examples.text: É assim que funciona.

translations.de: So funktioniert es.
translations.en: That's the way it works.
translations.fr: C'est comme ça que ça fonctionne.

more.definition: this way; like this (in this manner); thus (as a result)
more.etymology: From earlier assi, from Old Galician-Portuguese assi, from Late Latin ac sīc. Closely parallel to Aromanian ashi, Spanish así, Romanian așa. Compare also Catalan així, French ainsi, Italian così.

examples.text: Você nunca foi assim. Por que fez isso?

translations.de: So warst du noch nie. Warum hast du das getan?
translations.en: You were never like this. Why did you do that?
translations.fr: Tu n'as jamais été comme ça. Pourquoi as-tu fait ça ?

examples.text: A Lua é um assim chamado satélite natural.

translations.de: Der Mond ist ein sogenannter Trabant.
translations.en: The Moon is a so-called natural satellite.
translations.fr: La Lune est un satellite dit naturel.

examples.text: Por que eu não tenho um amigo assim?

translations.de: Warum habe ich nicht so einen Freund?
translations.en: Why don't I have a friend like that?
translations.fr: Pourquoi n'ai-je pas un ami comme ça ?

examples.text: Significa tanto assim para você?

translations.de: Bedeutet es dir wirklich so viel?
translations.en: Does it mean that much to you?
translations.fr: Cela compte-t-il tant pour vous ?

more.definition: well
more.etymology: From earlier assi, from Old Galician-Portuguese assi, from Late Latin ac sīc. Closely parallel to Aromanian ashi, Spanish así, Romanian așa. Compare also Catalan així, French ainsi, Italian così.

examples.text: A amizade é um amor que nunca morre.

translations.de: Freundschaft ist eine Liebe, die nie stirbt.
translations.en: Friendship is a love that never dies.
translations.fr: L'amitié est un amour qui ne meurt jamais.

examples.text: A terra nunca tinha sido arada.

translations.de: Das Land war noch nie gepflügt worden.
translations.en: The land had never been ploughed.
translations.fr: La terre n'avait jamais été labourée.

examples.text: Um homem honesto nunca rouba dinheiro.

translations.de: Ein ehrlicher Mann stiehlt nie Geld.
translations.en: An honest man never steals money.
translations.fr: Un honnête homme ne vole jamais d'argent.

examples.text: Não entre nunca nesse quarto.

translations.de: Betritt diesen Raum niemals.
translations.en: Never enter that room.
translations.fr: N'entrez jamais dans cette pièce.

more.definition: never (at no time; not ever)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese nunca, from Latin numquam (“never”).

examples.text: Você roubou meu coração e nunca o devolveu.

translations.de: Du hast mein Herz gestohlen und es nie zurückgegeben.
translations.en: You stole my heart and never gave it back.
translations.fr: Tu as volé mon cœur et tu ne me l'as jamais rendu.

examples.text: O que ela aprende não esquece nunca mais.

translations.de: Was sie lernt, vergisst sie nie.
translations.en: What she learns she never forgets.
translations.fr: Ce qu’elle apprend, elle ne l’oublie jamais.

examples.text: As ações dos mortais nunca escapam aos deuses.

translations.de: Die Taten der Sterblichen entgehen niemals den Göttern.
translations.en: The actions of mortals never escape the gods.
translations.fr: Les actions des mortels n'échappent jamais aux dieux.

examples.text: A mulher que eu amei nunca me amou.

translations.de: Die Frau, die ich liebte, hat mich nie geliebt.
translations.en: The woman I loved never loved me.
translations.fr: La femme que j'aimais ne m'a jamais aimé.

more.definition: neverness (the quality of not ever being extant or present)
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese nunca, from Latin numquam (“never”).

examples.text: Associo-me à senhora em alguns de seus pareceres.

translations.en: I agree with some of your opinions.

more.definition: expert opinion, advice, assessment, evaluation
more.etymology: Nominalization of Etymology 1.

examples.text: Esta frase parece estar gramaticalmente correta.

translations.de: Dieser Satz scheint grammatisch korrekt zu sein.
translations.en: This sentence seems to be grammatically correct.
translations.fr: Cette phrase semble être grammaticalement correcte.

examples.text: Ele não recusava desafios. Aceitava missões que pareciam impossíveis.

translations.de: Er hat nie eine Herausforderung abgelehnt. Er nahm Missionen an, die unmöglich schienen.
translations.en: He did not shy away from challenges. He accepted missions that seemed impossible.
translations.fr: Il n'a jamais refusé un défi. Il a accepté des missions qui semblaient impossibles.

examples.text: As zebras parecem cavalos listrados.

translations.de: Zebras sehen aus wie gestreifte Pferde.
translations.en: Zebras look like striped horses.
translations.fr: Les zèbres ressemblent à des chevaux rayés.

examples.text: Embora pareça impossível traduzir esse trocadilho, muita gente tenta!

translations.de: Obwohl es unmöglich erscheint, dieses Wortspiel zu übersetzen, versuchen es viele Leute!
translations.en: Although it seems impossible to translate this pun, many people try!
translations.fr: Bien qu'il semble impossible de traduire ce jeu de mots, beaucoup de gens essaient !

more.definition: to seem; to resemble
more.etymology: Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese parecer, from Vulgar Latin *pārēscere, from Latin pārēre.

senses.gloss: ter ares, aspecto de; dar a impressão de ser; aparentar

examples.text: Ele casou a filha com um homem rico.

translations.de: Er verheiratete seine Tochter mit einem reichen Mann.
translations.en: He married his daughter to a rich man.
translations.fr: Il a marié sa fille à un homme riche.

examples.text: Ele prometeu casar-se com ela.

translations.de: Er versprach, sie zu heiraten.
translations.en: He promised to marry her.
translations.fr: Il promit de l'épouser.

examples.text: Quero me casar com você.

translations.de: Ich will dich heiraten.
translations.en: I want to marry you.
translations.fr: Je veux t'épouser.

examples.text: Eu não gosto desse tipo de casa.

translations.de: Ich mag diese Art Haus nicht.
translations.en: I don't like this type of house.
translations.fr: Je n'aime pas ce genre de maison.

more.definition: to marry; to get married; to marry someone (unite two others in wedlock)
more.etymology: From Old Galician-Portuguese casar (13th century), probably from casa + -ar.

senses.gloss: ato de unir por casamento, por meio de processos jurídicos e/ou religiosos

examples.text: Ela partiu sem dizer por quê.

translations.de: Sie ging, ohne den Grund zu nennen.
translations.en: She left without saying why.
translations.fr: Elle est partie sans dire pourquoi.

examples.text: Você está louco ou o quê?

translations.de: Bist du verrückt oder was?
translations.en: Are you crazy, or what?
translations.fr: T'es dingue, ou quoi ?

examples.text: Eu posso usar o quê?

translations.de: Was kann ich benutzen?
translations.en: What can I use?
translations.fr: Que puis-je utiliser ?

examples.text: Sobre o quê ele está falando? Simplesmente não faz sentido.

translations.de: Über was spricht er? Es macht einfach keinen Sinn.
translations.en: What is he talking about? It just doesn't make sense.
translations.fr: De quoi parle-t-il ? Ça n'a simplement aucun sens.

examples.text: Não me pergunte por quê. Não me incomode assim. Acabou, ponto final.

translations.de: Frag mich nicht, warum. Nerv mich nicht so. Es ist vorbei, Punkt.
translations.en: Don't ask me why. Don't bother me like that. It's over, period.
translations.fr: Ne me demande pas pourquoi. Ne m'embête pas comme ça. C'est fini, point final.

more.definition: a characteristic (distinguishable feature of a person or thing); The name of the Latin script letter Q/q.
more.etymology: Inherited from Latin quem (“what”).
